Likewise, in the time of every messenger, it is not far-fetched that Allah cast the call into the hearts of a group of the jinn of his era, so they would hear his words, come to their people among the jinn, inform them of what they heard from the messengers, and warn them with it. Allah, may He be exalted, also called the messengers of Jesus His own messengers, saying: ﴿When We sent to them two﴾ [Ya-Sin: 14]. The clarification of this matter is that Allah, may He be exalted, rebuked the disbelievers with this verse only because He removed the excuse and cut off the pretext, by sending messengers to all, as bringers of good tidings and warners. When good tidings and warning reach everyone in this way, the purpose of removing the excuse and cutting off the pretext is achieved, and so the intended purpose is accomplished. Thus did al-Razi establish it.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: The evidence that the messengers were from mankind is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ [al-Nisa': 163], up to His saying: ﴿messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165], and His saying about Abraham: ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 27], thereby restricting prophethood and the Scripture after Abraham to his descendants. No one has said that prophethood existed among the jinn before Abraham and then ceased from them with his mission. And He said: ﴿We sent before you no messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], and He said: ﴿We sent before you none but men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the cities﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. It is known that the jinn follow mankind in this matter. End of quotation.

The second: If it is asked: What is the reason that they acknowledged disbelief in this verse, yet denied it in His saying: (p-2509) ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23]? We answer: The Day of Resurrection is a long day, and the states in it vary; at times they acknowledge, and at other times they deny. That indicates the intensity of their fear and the turmoil of their states, for whoever's fear is great, his speech becomes much disordered. This was conveyed by al-Razi.

Al-Zamakhshari added: Or what is meant is the testimony of their hands, feet, and skins, when a seal is placed upon their mouths.

The third: If it is asked: Why did He repeat the mention of their testimony against themselves? It is answered: The first is a report of their statement, how they speak and confess; the second is a censure of them, a rebuke of their opinion, and a description of the poverty of their reflection regarding themselves, and that they were a people deceived by the worldly life and its immediate pleasures. The outcome of their affair was that they were compelled to testify against themselves to disbelief, to submit to their Lord, and to deserve His punishment. He said this as a warning to listeners against the likes of their condition. Thus in the "Kashshaf."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 131:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:

[131] ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people were unaware.﴾

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people were unaware﴾ informs us that He, exalted is He, has left the two categories (jinn and humankind) without excuse by sending messengers, sending down scriptures, clarifying the signs, and establishing the proof through warning and threat. It also informs us that He, exalted is He, does not punish the cities for the injustice of their people, such as polytheism and the like, when a messenger has not reached them calling them to abandon it and alerting them to its falsehood, since that would contradict wisdom. It is permissible regarding this that it be the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., the matter is that. Or it is a subject whose predicate is omitted, i.e., as has been mentioned. Or its predicate is: "if your Lord would not..." etc. The referent is the coming of the messengers, or what has been recounted of their affair, or the question implied by His statement: "Did there not come to you..." Abu al-Su'ud favoured that the reference is to their testifying against themselves to disbelief and to deserving punishment, and that it is a subject whose predicate is what follows it, that "an" is verbal (masdariyyah), and that the "lam" is understood before it; or that it is light (mukhaffafah), its noun being the pronoun of the matter, and "bi-zulmin" is connected to "muhlik" (destroying), i.e., because of an injustice, or to an omitted element serving as a circumstantial clause (hal) from "al-qura" (the cities), i.e., characterized by injustice. The meaning: that is established because your Lord would not be [one who destroys the cities] on account of an injustice they committed before being alerted to its falsehood by a messenger.

Admonition:

In the verse is evidence that there is no obligation (taklif) before the sending of a messenger, and that reason has no ruling of its own, like His statement: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra' 15].

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[132] ﴿For each there are degrees according to what they have done, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do.﴾

﴿For each﴾ means: of those who are accountable (al-mukallafin, those bound by the obligations of the Law). ﴿Degrees﴾ means: ranks. ﴿According to what they have done﴾ means: according to their deeds, for which they are recompensed and rewarded, good for good and evil for evil. It has been cited, on this interpretation, as evidence that the jinn enter Paradise and are rewarded.

Ibn Kathir said: It is possible that His saying "For each" refers to the disbelievers among the jinn and humankind. That is, for each there is a degree in the Fire according to his deeds, as in His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of God, We will increase them in punishment upon punishment because of what they used to corrupt.﴾ [Al-Nahl: 88]

﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.﴾

[133] ﴿Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can remove you and grant succession to whomever He wills after you, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.﴾

﴿Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient﴾ free of need from all of His creation in every respect, while they are in need of Him in all their circumstances. ﴿The Possessor of mercy﴾, i.e., He shows mercy to them by imposing obligations upon them, to perfect them, and He grants them respite despite their disobedience. In this is an alert that what was mentioned before, of sending messengers, is not for His benefit, glory be to Him, but out of His mercy toward the servants, and it is a preparation for His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and grant succession to whomever He wills after you﴾, i.e., of creatures who act in obedience to Him: ﴿just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.﴾ He removed them and then their descendants, but He kept you alive out of mercy toward you. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient, and you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with a people other than you; then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[134] ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape it.﴾

﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾ means: of the Resurrection and its circumstances. ﴿is coming﴾ means: it will certainly occur without doubt. ﴿and you cannot escape it﴾ means: you cannot get away such that you could not be overtaken. This is a rebuttal of their saying: "Whoever dies has merely died." That is, He is able to restore you, even if you become dust and crumbled bones.

[١٣٥] ﴿Say, "O my people, act according to your position, and I too am acting. Soon you will know to whom the ultimate abode belongs. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾

﴿Say, "O my people, act according to your position"﴾ means: according to the utmost extent of your power and capacity. It is said: "makana makanatan" (مَكَنَ مَكانَةً) when one establishes himself to the fullest degree. Or it means: according to your manner and condition, from their saying "makan" and "makanah," like "maqam" and "maqamah." The meaning is: remain steadfast in your disbelief. ﴿I am acting﴾ means: in what I have been commanded, which is steadfastness upon Islam. ﴿Soon you will know to whom the ultimate abode belongs﴾ means: the abode that was built for the worship of Him alone, exalted is He, to the exclusion of others. Will it belong to the just one, who places worship in its proper place, or to the wrongdoer, who places it in other than its proper place? By "the abode" is meant the world (al-dunya), and by "the ultimate outcome" is meant the good outcome, that is, the outcome of goodness, because it is the original one. For He, exalted is He, made this world the field of the Hereafter and the bridge to it.

﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ means: the disbelievers. He placed "wrongdoing" in the place of "disbelief," indicating that the impossibility of success follows from any individual kind of wrongdoing, so what then of disbelief, which is the greatest of its kinds?

Subtleties (lata'if):

In presenting the threat in the form of a command, namely His saying ﴿act according to your position﴾, there is exaggeration in the warning, as if the one threatening wishes to punish him, having resolved upon it, so he compels him by the command to what leads to it. And there is a recording that the one threatened can only produce evil, like one commanded to do something he cannot avoid.

In His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Soon you will know﴾, together with the warning, there is fairness in speech and good manners, since he did not say "the outcome is for us" but entrusted the matter to God. This is from fair speech, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed either we or you are upon guidance or in clear error﴾ [Saba': 24].

In it is an indication of the warner's certainty that he is in the right.

In it is also good news that the outcome belongs to him.

Ibn Kathir said: God has fulfilled His promise to His Messenger, may the blessings of God be upon him. He established him in the lands, made him ruler over the necks of his opponents among the servants, opened Mecca for him, and gave him victory over those of his people who denied him, opposed him, and were hostile to him. His affairs became firm over all the Arabian Peninsula, likewise Yemen and Bahrain, and all of that during his lifetime. Then the cities, regions and districts (al-rasatiq) were conquered after his death, in the days of his successors, may God be pleased with them all, as (p-2513) God, exalted is He, said: ﴿God has decreed, "I and My messengers will surely prevail. Indeed God is Powerful and Mighty"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51], ﴿the day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 52]. And God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers"﴾ [Ibrahim: 13], ﴿and We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing and fears My threat﴾ [Ibrahim: 14]. And God, exalted is He, said: ﴿God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the land, as He made successors those before them, and He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and He will surely change their state after their fear into security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ [al-Nur: 55]. And God, exalted is He, has done that for this community, and to Him belong praise and grace.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 136:

Then Exalted is He explained a kind of the ignorance and misguidance of the polytheists of Makkah: their giving preference to the idols (asnam) over Him, glorified be He, after associating them with Him in what is exclusive to His creation. [He did so] by His saying, glorified be He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His Exalted saying:

[136] ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "this is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, and what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge.﴾

﴿And they assign to Allah from what He created﴾ i.e., created: ﴿of the crops﴾ i.e., the produce: ﴿and livestock a share﴾ (p-2514) which they devote to guests and the needy. I.e., and for their idols they assign a share which they devote to worship and to the custodians (sadana) [of the idols]. It was not mentioned [explicitly] because what follows suffices.

﴿They say, "This is for Allah, by their claim"﴾ with a fatha and with a damma (al-Shihab said: al-za'm is triptote, like al-wudd). I.e., this is now firmly assigned to Him, without its being firmly assigned to Him in the future, which is subject to change. ﴿And this is for our partners﴾, and it is firmly assigned to them, indeed what is not theirs also becomes firmly theirs. So whenever something fell from Allah's share into their partners' share they picked it up, or whenever something from their partners' share fell into His share they left it, as Exalted is He said: ﴿So what is for their partners does not reach Allah﴾, i.e., at its growth or its falling into what is for Allah. Or the destruction of what is for Allah does not reach the purposes to which they devoted it, such as the hospitality of guests and charity to the needy. ﴿And what is for Allah reaches their partners﴾, i.e., at its growth or its falling into what is for the idols, or the destruction of their property, so they spend on them, by slaughtering sacrifices at them, providing for their custodians, and the like. They justified this by saying that Allah is self-sufficient while they are in need: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, i.e., what they apportion; for first they did what had not been prescribed for them, and they went astray in the division, because He, Exalted is He, is the Lord of everything, its Sovereign and its Creator, there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him. Then, when they made what they claimed was a division, which was corrupt, they did not preserve it, but acted unjustly in it, since they gave preference to the side of the idols in guarding and safekeeping, out of foolishness.

Al-Mahayimi said: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, i.e., [the giving of] preference to the side of the idols over the side of Allah, with a reason that calls for preferring the side of Allah because of His divinity, and the unsuitability of the idols for divinity together with their need.

What we have mentioned concerning the verse is what the leading scholars of tafsir have said.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said regarding the interpretation of this verse: The enemies of Allah, whenever they sowed a crop, or had a fruit, would assign to Allah a portion of it and to the idol a portion. Whatever was of the crop or fruit or some of the share of the idols, they guarded and counted. If something fell from it into what was designated for the True One, they returned it to what they had assigned to the idol. If the water that was assigned to the idol overtook some of what was assigned to Allah and watered it, they assigned that to the idol. If something of the crop and fruit assigned to Allah fell and mixed with what was assigned to the idol, they said, "This is poor," and did not return it to what they had assigned to Allah. If the water assigned to Allah overtook and watered what was designated for the idol, they left it for the idol. They used to forbid from their property the bahirah, the sa'ibah, the wasilah and the ham, and they would assign them to the idols, claiming they forbade them as an act of devotion to Allah, Exalted is He. So He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And they assign to Allah from what He created﴾, the verse.

Ibn Kathir said: Likewise said Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others besides them.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[137] ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to bring them to ruin and to confuse them regarding their religion. And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and what they invent.﴾

﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾ That is, in the same way as that adornment, namely the adornment of polytheism in the division mentioned earlier, their allies among the devils made attractive to them something even more hideous in the matter of sacrifices: the killing of their children for fear of poverty, and the burying of daughters alive for fear of shame. The devils were called "partners" only because they obeyed them in what they commanded them concerning the killing of their children, so they made them partners with Allah in the obligation of obeying them. ﴿To bring them to ruin﴾ That is, to destroy them through polytheism and the killing of the child, from (al-irda', which linguistically means destruction). ﴿And to confuse them regarding their religion﴾ That is, to mix up for them what they were upon with the religion of Abraham regarding the sacrifice of Ishmael, peace be upon them both; or with what it was obligatory for them to hold as religion, because they were upon the religion of Ishmael. So this one who brought them these corrupt practices wanted to turn them away from that true religion. ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so﴾ That is, do not grieve over their destruction by what they do, for it occurs by the will of Allah. ﴿So leave them and what they invent﴾ That is, because for Him, in what He wills, there are far-reaching wisdoms: ﴿Indeed, We give them respite only that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 178]. And in this there is a severity of warning that is not hidden.

Note:

"Their partners" is the subject of "made attractive," placed after the adverbial phrase and the object for the sake of emphasizing and giving importance to what is put first, because it is the point of wonder, since they put the more important first, and those concerned with it are more so. Ibn 'Amir alone read "zuyyina" in the passive voice, with the killing as the subject, "awlad" in the accusative, and "shurakai'" in the genitive by annexing the killing to it, separated between them by its object. Al-Zamakhshari, may Allah pardon him, rejected this reading and counted it among the great errors of his Kashshaf, where he said: "As for the reading of Ibn 'Amir, it is something which, even if it were in a place of necessity, namely poetry, would be ugly and rejected, as the following was ugly and rejected:

"He drove the she-camel, the father of Mazada"

How then would it be in prose? How then would it be in the Qur'an, which is inimitable in the beauty of its arrangement and its eloquence?" He said: "What led him to that is that he saw in some copies 'shurakaihim' written with a ya', and had he read the children and the partners in the genitive, since the children are their partners in their wealth, he would have found in that an alternative to this resort." End.

Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: Al-Zamakhshari has indeed mounted the back of a blind [camel], and wandered in a desert waste, and I disown before Allah, and I clear of it the bearers of His Book and the preservers of His speech, what he has accused them of. For he imagined that the readers, the imams of the seven readings, each chose a letter to read by personal reasoning (ijtihad), not by transmission and hearing. For this reason, he thought Ibn 'Amir erred in this reading, and began to show that the cause of his error was seeing the ya' firmly present in (shurakaihim), so it was inferred that it is genitive, and the accusative of (awladuhum) became fixed for him by analogy, since a verbal noun is not annexed to two things at once, so he read it in the accusative. He said: He had an alternative to its accusative, namely its genitive by annexation, and making "the partners" a substitute for it, and that would have been better than what he resorted to. All of this, as you see, is a supposition of al-Zamakhshari that Ibn 'Amir read this reading by his own opinion, whereas the correct view was otherwise and the eloquent is other than it. Al-Zamakhshari did not know that this reading, with the accusative of the children and the separation between the annexed and the annexed-to by it, is known by necessity to have been recited by the Prophet ﷺ as it was revealed to him by Jibril, and then the Prophet ﷺ recited it to the number of transmitters of the mass-transmission (tawatur) among the imams, and the number of mass-transmission continued passing it on and reciting it, generation after generation, until it reached Ibn 'Amir, who also read it as he heard it. This is the belief of the people of truth regarding all seven readings: that they are mass-transmitted in whole and in detail from the most eloquent of those who spoke Arabic, ﷺ. So when you know the correct creed, there is no concern after it with the words of al-Zamakhshari, nor with the words of his likes who considered Ibn 'Amir's reading a grammatical error, for the one who objected to it only objected to what is established as clearly and necessarily free of error. Were it not for the excuse that the objector is not among the people of the two disciplines, I mean the science of recitation and the science of the principles, and is not counted among those of the two mentioned fields, it would be feared that he had left the bond of religion. Yet by this excuse he is in a perilous obligation and an abhorrent slip, exceeding the slip of one who thinks that the details of the seven readings include what is not mass-transmitted, for this speaker did not establish them except by transmission, and his ultimate claim is that their transmission does not require mass-transmission. As for al-Zamakhshari, he thought they are established by opinion, not depending on transmission, and no one among the Muslims has said this. What led him to this fancy is only excessive belief in the consistency of grammatical analogies, so he took them to be definitive, until whatever contradicts them is brought. Then, even if one grants him the consistency of the analogy he claimed to be consistent, Ibn 'Amir's reading does not contradict it. For the separation between the annexed and the annexed-to, although difficult, yet when a verbal noun is annexed to its object, it is estimated as a verb, and by this estimation it governs. And although its annexation is not pure (ghayr mahḍa), it is likened to what has a non-pure annexation, to the point that some grammarians said its annexation is not pure. Therefore, the outcome is that its connection to the annexed-to is not like the connection of others, and separation has come between an annexed non-verbal noun and its annexed-to by an adverb, so at least the verbal noun should be distinguished from others, for what we have explained of its detachment in estimation, and its not going deep into connection, such that it may be separated between it and the annexed-to by what is not foreign to it. It is as if, in estimation, one unties it into a verb, then fronts the object before the subject, annexes it to the subject, and the object remains in its place at the time of untying. What also facilitates this is the variation in the state of the verbal noun, for at times it is annexed to the subject and at times to the object. Some have restricted the permissibility of separation by the object between it and the subject, because it occurs out of its proper position, since the intention is delay, so it is as if it did not separate. Just as it is permissible for the pronoun to precede the noun when it comes out of its rank, because the intention with it is delay. Abu 'Ubayda recited:

"So he trampled them with the trampling of the threshing threshers"

He also recited:

"They rub the grain of the cone-shaped ear in the plain, like the rubbing of ginned cotton"

So he separated, as you see, between the verbal noun and the subject by the object. And among what strengthens that its annexation is not deep is the permissibility of coordinating on the place of its genitive, in nominative and accusative. All these are points supported by rules and illustrated by evidences from the analogies of Arabic, gathering the scattered grammatical principles for this reading. Our aim is not to correct the reading by the rules of Arabic, but to correct the rules of Arabic by the reading. This is sufficient, if Allah wills, in combining the two, and Allah is the Granter of success. What we have treated in the course of the discussion regarding bringing close the annexation of the verbal noun that is not pure, we only intended its joining with other aspects by which, through their combination, it is shown that the separation is not objectionable in its annexation nor far-fetched from analogy; and we did not isolate it as a proof of the stated point, for what is agreed upon as not being pure does not permit separation in it, so the aspect mentioned cannot stand alone as proof. And Allah is the Granter of success. End of the words of al-Nasir, may Allah have mercy on him.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained another kind of their fabrications by His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[138] ﴿And they say, "These are livestock and tilth set apart; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim, and there are livestock whose backs have been forbidden, and livestock over which they do not mention the name of Allah, a fabrication against Him. He will surely recompense them for what they used to fabricate.﴾

﴿And they say, "These are﴾ a reference to what they had designated for their gods, and the feminine form is for the matter (khabar) being referred to: ﴿livestock and tilth set apart (hijr)﴾, i.e., forbidden. (The majority read the ḥāʼ with a kasra and the jīm with a sukūn.) It is a form (fiʻl) in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ūl), like dhibḥ (slaughtered) and ṭaḥn (ground), in that both masculine and feminine, singular and plural, are described by it equally, because its ruling is that of nouns rather than adjectives. That is: forbidden to us, or restricted from our wealth for the idols. It is also read with a ḍammah on the ḥāʼ.

(p-٢٥٢١) ﴿None may eat of them except whom we wish﴾. In al-Madārik it says: when they designated certain items from their tilth and livestock for the gods, they would say, "None may eat of them except whom we wish," meaning: the servants of the idols, and men, but not women.

﴿By their claim﴾ is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) from the subject of "they say," i.e., clinging to their false claim without any proof.

Ibn Kathir said: This noble verse is like His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you made from it [some] unlawful and [some] lawful? Say: Has Allah permitted you, or do you fabricate against Allah?﴾ [Yunus: 59].

﴿And livestock﴾ meaning: they said, pointing to another group of their livestock: "These are livestock ﴿whose backs have been forbidden﴾," meaning by them the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah and the ḥām: ﴿and livestock over which they do not mention the name of Allah﴾, i.e., at the time of slaughter; rather they mention over them the names of the idols. ﴿A fabrication against Him﴾, i.e., against Allah, and a lie on their part in attributing this to the religion and law of Allah, for He never permitted them to do so, nor was He pleased with it from them. ﴿He will surely recompense them for what they used to fabricate﴾, i.e., against Him, attributing it to Him. In this is a warning and a threat.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 139:

Then the Exalted explained another kind of their misguidance through His saying, glory be to Him:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[139] ﴿And they say, "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females; but if it is dead, then they are equal partners in it. He will surely recompense them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing."﴾

﴿And they say, "What is in the wombs of these livestock"﴾ meaning the fetuses of the baheerahs and the saa'ibahs: ﴿"exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females"﴾ meaning that it is lawful for males only, not for females, if it is born alive, according to His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿"but if it is dead"﴾, i.e., what is in their wombs, ﴿"then they are equal partners in it"﴾, so males and females are alike in it.

In the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, the intended meaning of ﴿"what is in their wombs"﴾ is the milk. They used to forbid it to their females, and their males would drink it. When a she-goat gave birth to a male, they would slaughter it, and it was for the men only, not the women. If it was a female, it was left and not slaughtered, and if it was dead, they were equal partners in it.

Al-Sha'bi said: As for the baheerah, only the men would eat from its milk, and if any of it died, both men and women would eat it. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and Ibn Aslam.

﴿"He will surely recompense them for their description"﴾, i.e., for the lawful and unlawful declared arbitrarily and attributed to Allah, the Exalted: ﴿"Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing"﴾, i.e., Wise in His acts, sayings and legislation, Knowing of the deeds of His servants, whether good or evil, and He will recompense them for them.

Note:

al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil": Malik took as evidence His saying: ﴿"exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females"﴾ that it is not permissible to make an endowment (waqf) exclusively for one's male children to the exclusion of daughters, and that such an endowment is annulled, even after the death of the endower, because that is an act of the Jahiliyyah. Some of the Malikis used it as evidence for the same ruling regarding gifts (hibah). End of quote.

Subtleties:

The (ta') in ﴿khaalisatun﴾ is either for transferring the word to the status of a noun, or for emphasis, or because "al-khaalisah" is a verbal noun like "al-'aafiyah," placed in the position of "al-khaalis" for emphasis, or by omitting a modified noun, i.e., "dhu khaalisatin" (possessor of exclusivity), or for the feminine gender based on the view that "ma" refers to the fetuses. The masculine in ﴿muharram﴾ is in consideration of the wording. It has also been read as ﴿khaalisatan﴾ in the accusative, as an emphatic infinitive, with the predicate being ﴿lidhukurinaa﴾. Their description occupies the position of the infinitive of ﴿sayajziihim﴾, with an elided modified noun; i.e., the recompense of their description of the lie against Him, exalted is He, regarding the forbidding and permitting, from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿"And their tongues describe the lie"﴾ [al-Nahl: 62].

al-Shihab said: This is from the eloquent and wondrous speech, for they say: "the description of his speech is a lie" when he lies, and "his eye describes magic," meaning it is magical, and "he describes agility," meaning he is agile, as an intensification, to the point that whoever hears or sees him seems to be described to him in a way that explains it. al-Ma'arri said:

"The lightning of al-Ma'arrah passed after a weakness, so it spent the night at Ramah describing the weariness."

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 140:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[140] ﴿Those have lost who killed their children in foolishness without knowledge, and forbade what Allah had provided for them, fabricating [lies] against Allah. They have certainly gone astray, and they were not guided.﴾

﴿Those have lost who killed their children﴾ meaning: burying their daughters alive, out of fear of captivity or poverty. ﴿in foolishness without knowledge﴾ due to the lightness of their minds and their ignorance that Allah is the provider of their children, not they themselves.

﴿and forbade what Allah had provided for them﴾ of the bahira, the sa'iba and the like: ﴿fabricating [lies] against Allah. They have certainly gone astray﴾ from the straight path, ﴿and they were not guided﴾ i.e., to the truth and what is right.

Al-Shihab said: In His saying ﴿and they were not guided﴾ after His saying ﴿They have certainly gone astray﴾ there is an emphasis on negating guidance from them, because the form of the verb requires that straying occurs after it had not been. Therefore it is followed by this state, to clarify their deep entrenchment in error, and their newly arisen error is [like] darkness, layer upon layer.

(p-2524) Reminder:

Many exegetes understood "loss" to encompass both abodes. As for this world, they lost the benefits of their children and the fruit of what they were created for; likewise the benefits of their livestock, by what they restricted and prohibited in them through innovation. As for the Hereafter, they will arrive at the worst of abodes. And this generalization, although it is true, the more apparent reading is to restrict it to the Hereafter, in harmony with similar passages, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed﴾ [Yunus: 69] ﴿A brief enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 70].

Al-Hafiz Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: If it pleases you to know the ignorance of the Arabs, then recite what comes after the one hundred and thirtieth verse of Surat al-An'am: ﴿Those have lost who killed their children﴾, the verse. Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it in "Manaqib Quraysh" in his Sahih.

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[141] "It is He who produces gardens, both trellised and untrellised, and palm trees and crops of varying produce, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive."

His words, Exalted is He: "It is He who produces gardens, both trellised and untrellised" are a preface to what will come of the detailed description of the conditions of livestock. That is: He is the One who bestowed upon you kinds of blessings, so that you would worship Him alone. So He created for you orchards of vines and others, trellised, i.e., supported by the posts you set up for them. It is said: "I trellised the vine" when you provide it with supports and a framework upon which the shoots are trained. "And untrellised" means left spread upon the surface of the earth, not trellised. "And" He produced the palm tree bearing fruit, for it is both fruit and staple food. "And the crops," which yield various kinds of staple food, "of varying produce" i.e., their fruit and grain differ in color, taste, size and fragrance. "And olives and pomegranates, similar" in color and shape, and their leaves, "and dissimilar" in taste. "Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit" i.e., eat of the fruit of each of what has been mentioned, when it ripens.

Al-Razi said: When He, Exalted is He, mentioned the manner of His creating these things, He mentioned the actual purpose of creating them, which is the benefit of the accountable ones from them, so He said: "Eat of their fruit." And they differed concerning what the benefit of this is. Some of them said: it is permission. Others said: rather, the purpose of it is permission to eat before the right (ḥaqq) is paid, because when He made the right obligatory upon it, it could have been forbidden for the owner to take from it, due to the partnership of the poor in it. Rather, this is the apparent meaning. So He, Exalted is He, permitted this eating, and removed the obligation of the right from being a barrier to this disposal. Some of them said: Rather, Exalted is He permitted that to clarify that the purpose of creating these blessings is either eating or giving charity, and He mentioned eating before giving charity because caring for oneself takes precedence over caring for others. He, Exalted is He, said: "And do not forget your share of this world, and do good as Allah has done good to you" [al-Qasas: 77]. End.

"And give its due on the day of its harvest": it is read with a fatḥah and with a kasrah on the ḥā'. This is a command to give to whoever is present on that day what is easily available, and it is not the obligatory zakat, so said ʿAṭāʾ, i.e., because the sūrah is Makkan, and zakat was only made obligatory in Madinah. Likewise Mujāhid said: When the needy are present with you, you cast for them some of it. In another narration from him: At the harvest he gives a handful, and at the reaping he gives a handful and leaves them to follow the traces of the reapers. This is also narrated from Nāfiʿ, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi and others. According to these, this right remains and was not abrogated by zakat, so they make it obligatory to feed whoever attends the harvest on the basis of this verse. Among what supports this is that He, Exalted is He, censured those who cut and do not give charity, when He related to us the evil of their deed and His retribution upon them. He, Exalted is He, said in the sūrah of (Nūn): "When they swore they would surely harvest it in the morning" [al-Qalam: 17] "and did not make exception" [al-Qalam: 18] "Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord while they were sleeping" [al-Qalam: 19] "So it became like the darkened [harvest]" [al-Qalam: 20], i.e., like the dark night, black and burned, "Then they called to one another in the morning" [al-Qalam: 21] "Go early to your crops if you are going to harvest" [al-Qalam: 22] "So they set out while speaking in secret" [al-Qalam: 23] "No needy person will enter it today upon you" [al-Qalam: 24], and the verses.

Some of them held that this right was abrogated by the verse of zakat; Ibn Jarir related this from Ibn ʿAbbas and a group of the Successors. Ibn Kathir said: There is a problem with calling this abrogation, because it was already an obligatory matter. Then he explained its clarification and specified the amount of what is to be given and its quantity. End.

There is no problem with this, given what you have learned in the introduction about calling such things abrogation according to the early scholars, and it passed shortly before as well, so remember!

Some of them held that the verse is Madinan, added to this sūrah among its counterparts, which we explained at the beginning of the sūrah, and that the right is the obligatory zakat. It is related from Anas, Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn al-Musayyab.

The command to give it on the day of harvest is for emphasis on resolving to hasten to it. The meaning: resolve to give the right, intend it, and be concerned with it on the day of the harvest, so that you do not delay it beyond the first time when giving is possible. Al-Hakim said: It was said: The time of harvest was mentioned only to lighten the burden on the owners, so what is eaten before it is not counted against them.

Al-ʿAwfi related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: A man, when he sowed and his day of harvest came, would not give out anything from what he harvested, so He, Exalted is He, said: "And give its due on the day of its harvest," and that is so that he knows its measure and its right, which is one out of every ten, and what people pick up of its ears.

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud related from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered from every owner of a palm-garden ten wasqs of dates, in a cluster hung in the mosque for the needy."

Ibn Kathir said: Its chain is good and strong.

Note:

In al-Iklil it says: Those who held that zakat is obligatory on every crop and fruit used this verse as evidence, especially olives and pomegranates, which are mentioned explicitly. Those who restricted it to grains said: harvest is literally applied only to these. Also in it is evidence that zakat is not required to be paid before the harvest. It was also cited as evidence that conjunction does not necessarily produce equality in rulings, because He, Exalted is He, joined eating, which is not obligatory by consensus, with giving, which is obligatory by consensus. End.

His words, Exalted is He: "And do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive" are a prohibition of excess, either in giving charity, i.e., do not give beyond what is reasonable. Abu al-ʿAliyah said: They used to give something on the day of harvest, then they competed in it and went to excess, so "And do not be excessive" was revealed. Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who harvested a palm-grove of his and said: "No one will come to me today except that I will feed him." So he fed until evening and had no fruit left, and it was revealed. Hence al-Suddi said: i.e., do not give away your wealth so that you end up sitting in poverty. Or it refers to eating before the harvest; this is from Abu Muslim, who said: Do not be excessive in eating before the harvest, lest it lead to diminishing the right of the poor. Or it refers to everything; ʿAtaʾ said: They were forbidden from excess in everything. Iyas ibn Muʿawiyah said: Whatever you exceed the command of Allah with, that is excess. Ibn Jarir chose the view of ʿAtaʾ. Ibn Kathir said: There is no doubt that it is correct, but the apparent meaning, Allah knows best, from the context of the verse, where He, Exalted is He, said: "Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit," is that it refers to eating. That is: do not be excessive in eating, because of the harm it causes to the mind and body, like His words, Exalted is He: "Eat and drink, but do not be excessive" [al-Aʿraf: 31], the verse... 

In Sahih al-Bukhari, as a suspended narration: "Eat, drink, dress, and give charity, without excess or pride." This is from this, Allah knows best. End.

Al-Mahayimi also inclined to this in his tafsir, where he said: "And do not be excessive in eating them, lest by satisfying desires you nullify the purpose of the cultivation."

Then Allah (Exalted) described the condition of the cattle, and refuted what they had invented about them concerning prohibition and permission, by His saying:

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[142] ﴿And of the cattle, some for burden and some for flesh. Eat of what Allah has provided for you and do not follow the steps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾

﴿And of the cattle, some for burden and some for flesh﴾ That is: He produced for you, from the cattle, that which carries loads, and that which is spread out for slaughter (i.e., laid down), or from whose wool, fleece and hair carpets are woven.

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "The burden-bearers (ḥamūlah) are the large animals fit for carrying, and the carpet (farsh) is the small ones, such as the young camels, the calves and the sheep, because they are close to the ground, owing to the lightness of their bodies, like the spread carpet laid upon it." So on the first two interpretations, farsh means "that which is spread (maftūsh)"; and on the third, the speech is a figure of comparison (tashbīh).

﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you﴾ That is: of the fruits, the crops and the cattle, for preserving life and for increasing strength.

﴿And do not follow the steps of Satan﴾ That is: his commands concerning permission and prohibition, as the people of the Jahiliyyah followed them, so they prohibited what Allah had provided for them, inventing lies against Him, as has passed.

﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾ That is: manifestly hostile, who prevents you from what preserves your lives and increases your strength, and who calls you to fabricate lies against Allah by attributing them to His command, or to claim divinity for yourselves if you were to act independently with it.

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[143] ﴿Eight pairs: two of the sheep and two of the goats. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful.﴾

His words, exalted is He, ﴿Eight pairs﴾ are in apposition to ﴿livestock for burden and for hides﴾ [al-An'am: 142], or they are the object of (kulu, "eat"). (Wa la tattabi'u, "and do not follow"), which comes between them, is either a parenthetical clause, or a verb implied by what precedes it, or a circumstantial phrase (hal) relating to (ma), meaning "varied" or "of various kinds." A zawj (pair) is that which has with it another of its own kind to pair with it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female﴾ [al-Najm: 45]. It may also be said of the two together, but the first meaning is intended.

﴿Of the sheep﴾, two: ﴿two﴾, the ram and the ewe; ﴿and of the goats, two﴾, the he-goat and the she-goat. ﴿Say﴾, that is, as a rebuke to them and to show their inability to answer: ﴿the two males﴾ of the sheep and the goats: ﴿has He forbidden﴾ to you, O polytheists? Or ﴿the two females﴾ of them? ﴿Or what the wombs of the two females contain﴾, that is, or what the females of both kinds have carried, whether male or female, as they said: ﴿What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males﴾ [al-An'am: 139], and the verse continues.

﴿Inform me with knowledge﴾, that is, with a transmitted proof from the books of the earliest messengers, or a rational proof in distinguishing between these two kinds and the two kinds that follow. This is what al-Mahayimi said.

﴿If you are truthful﴾, that is, in your claim of prohibition.

In His words, exalted is He, ﴿Inform me with knowledge﴾ there is a repetition of the demand for evidence and a reiteration of the rebuke and the silencing.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[144] ﴿And of camels two, and of cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you? So who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to mislead people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

﴿And of camels two﴾ is conjoined to His saying: ﴿of sheep two﴾ [al-An'am: 143], meaning: and He produced from the camels two, namely the male camel and the female camel, and from cattle two, a male and a female. ﴿Say﴾, meaning: silencing them also regarding these two kinds: ﴿the two males﴾ of them ﴿has He forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?﴾, meaning: of those two kinds. The meaning is a denial that Allah, glorified and exalted, forbade them any of the four types, and a demonstration of their lying in that. The detailing of what was mentioned of the males and females and what is in their bellies is for the sake of emphasis in refuting them, by bringing denial upon every substance of their fabrications. For they used to forbid the males of the livestock at one time, their females at another time, and their offspring however they were at yet another time, all while attributing that entirely to Allah, glorified. The reason he followed the detailing of each of the two kinds of young and the two kinds of adults with the command in the form of interrogation and denial mentioned, together with the rebuke that comes from stating the command after the detailing of the four types, is that one would say: "Say: Has the males forbidden, or the females, or what the wombs of the females contain?" — because of the emphasis and binding force that lies in the duality and repetition. This was stated by Abu al-Su'ud.

Then He repeated the silencing with His saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses﴾, present: ﴿when Allah enjoined this upon you﴾, meaning: when He enjoined upon you the forbidding of some and the permitting of others. This is by way of mockery: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, meaning: who attributes to Him the forbidding of what He did not forbid: ﴿to mislead people without knowledge﴾, meaning: without evidence. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ Ibn Kathir said: The first to enter into this verse was 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah, for he was the first to alter the religion of the prophets, the first to release the sawa'ib (free-roaming animals), the first to make the wasilah (a she-camel whose offspring is withheld), and the first to make the hami (a stallion protected from work) a protected animal, as is established in the Sahih.

(Abu al-Su'ud said: The intended are their elders who acknowledged this; or 'Amr ibn Luhayy, who was the founder of this evil; or all of them, for their shared fabrication against Him, glorified and exalted.)

A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: How did He separate some of the counted items from others without continuing them together? I say: The separation between them occurred as a parenthetical insertion not foreign to the counted items. That is because Allah, mighty and majestic, bestowed upon His servants by producing the livestock for their benefits and permitting them to them. So there was an interjection with argument against those who forbade them. Argument against those who forbid them is an affirmation and a confirmation of the permission. And interjections in speech are only employed for emphasis. End.

A note:

The verse indicates the permissibility of eating the flesh of livestock, which is known as a matter of religion by necessity; likewise benefiting by riding what is ridden, and using their wool, hair and hides as coverings, and refuting what the Jahiliyyah used to forbid without knowledge.

Al-Mu'ayyad billah said: The domesticated and the wild enter into His saying: ﴿of sheep two and of goats two﴾ [al-An'am: 143]. It was answered that His saying: ﴿eight pairs﴾ [al-An'am: 143] is an explanation of the livestock, and the term "al-an'am" is not applied to the wild. This was stated by one of the Zaydi exegetes.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, commanded His Messenger ﷺ—after the polytheists had been held to account, rebuked, and shown that what they fabricated concerning prohibition was pure invention—to make clear to them what He had prohibited for them, so He, glory be to Him, said:

(p-2533) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[145] ﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, except that it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine—for indeed it is an abomination—or a sinful offering over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked. But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden"﴾ That is: forbidden food among the foods. ﴿to an eater﴾ That is: an eater, whether male or female. This is a response to their saying, "It is forbidden for our wives," and His saying ﴿who would eat it﴾ serves to add emphasis. ﴿except that it be﴾ That is: that food being ﴿carrion﴾. Al-Mahayimi said: Death is the cause of corruption, so it is defiling, unless some preventing factor blocks its effect, such as the mention of Allah's name, or its being from water, or other things. ﴿or blood poured forth﴾ That is: flowing, not the liver or the spleen. ﴿or the flesh of swine—for indeed it is an abomination﴾ Because of its habit of eating filth. ﴿or a sinful offering﴾ That is: a departure from the religion, which is like a purifying life. ﴿over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked﴾ That is: slaughtered in the name of idols, and the voice was raised over its slaughter in the name of other than Allah. That which was invoked over for other than Allah is called "sinful" only because it plunges deeply into the category of sin, and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is sinful﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. ﴿But whoever is compelled﴾ That is: whom necessity has afflicted, driving him to consume something of what has been mentioned. ﴿neither desiring﴾ That is: against another compelled person like himself, abandoning his sharing with him. ﴿nor transgressing﴾ Exceeding the measure of his need from consuming it. ﴿then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ He does not hold him to account. The explanation of this verse has already been given in Surah al-Baqarah and al-Ma'idah, in what suffices.

Remarks:

The first: Ibn Kathir said: The purpose of the context of this noble verse is the refutation of the polytheists who innovated what they innovated of prohibiting the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah, the ham, and the like. So Allah, Exalted is He, commanded His Messenger to inform them that he does not find in what was revealed to him that these are forbidden, and that what He has forbidden is carrion and what is mentioned with it. (p-2534) And beyond that, nothing was forbidden; it is only a pardoned matter about which silence is kept. So how do you claim it is unlawful? From where have you forbidden it when Allah, Exalted is He, did not forbid it? On this basis, it does not negate the prohibition of other things after this, as the prohibition of the flesh of domestic donkeys, the flesh of predators, and every clawed bird of prey has come—end quote. In sum, the verse indicates that the Prophet ﷺ did not find in what was revealed to him, up to that limit, anything other than these. And it is not contradicted by the occurrence of prohibition afterward of other things, such as the strangled animal, the animal beaten to death, the one fallen from a height, the one gored, and others. That is because this surah is Meccan, so whatever else was later made forbidden in it is a subsequent addition. It was said: if something other than what is mentioned is forbidden, it would be abrogation of what this verse implies regarding its permissibility. Its answer: that is an increase in prohibition, not abrogation of what is in the verse. Thus the prohibition of every animal with fangs among predators and every clawed bird is established. Some people call this abrogation in the Salafi sense, and we have explained this repeatedly.

Some of the Zaydis said: Ibn 'Abbas held to the verse in permitting the flesh of domestic donkeys, and 'A'ishah held to it regarding the flesh of predators, and 'Ikrimah regarding the permissibility of everything except what is in the verse. And it is related from al-Sha'bi that he would permit the flesh of the elephant and recite this verse.

None of them has a valid basis in the verse, because Allah, Exalted is He, clarified what is prohibited in those circumstances—end quote.

As-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: Many of the early scholars cited it to permit what is not mentioned in it. Among that is the domestic donkey, which al-Bukhari related from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I said to Jabir ibn Zayd: "They claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade domestic donkeys." He said: "al-Hakam ibn 'Amr al-Ghifari used to say that among us in Basra. But that sea (Ibn 'Abbas) refused it," and he recited: (p-2535) ﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me"﴾ the verse.

Abu Dawud related from Ibn 'Umar that he was asked about eating the hedgehog, so he recited: ﴿Say: "I do not find"﴾ the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim and others related with a sound chain from 'A'ishah that whenever she was asked about every animal with fangs among predators and every clawed bird, she recited: ﴿Say: "I do not find"﴾ the verse.

And he related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: There is nothing forbidden among animals except what Allah has forbidden in His Book: ﴿Say: "I do not find"﴾ the verse. End quote.

Abu Dawud related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to eat some things and leave others out of disgust. So Allah sent His Prophet ﷺ, revealed His Book, made lawful what is lawful and forbade what is unlawful. So what He made lawful is lawful, what He forbade is unlawful, and what He was silent about is pardoned. And he recited: ﴿Say: "I do not find"﴾ the verse.

We have mentioned the weakness of relying on this verse for what they went to.

In Fath al-Bayan: The meaning of the verse is that Allah, Exalted is He, commanded His Messenger ﷺ to inform them that he does not find in what was revealed to him any prohibition other than these mentioned items. This indicates that the prohibited things are confined to them, were it not that it is Meccan. Surah al-Ma'idah was revealed after it at Medina, and to these prohibitions were added: the strangled, the beaten, the fallen, and the gored. And it is authentically related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the prohibition of every animal with fangs among predators (p-2536) and every clawed bird, and the prohibition of domestic donkeys and dogs, and the like.

In sum, if this generality concerns what is eaten of animals, as the context indicates and the exception confirms, then every subsequent indication in the Book or Sunnah that shows the prohibition of some animal is added to it. And if this generality concerns everything Allah has forbidden of animals and other things, then every subsequent indication of prohibition of some thing is added to it. It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, and 'A'ishah that there is no prohibition except what Allah mentioned in this verse, and this was related from Malik. This is a fallen view and an extremely weak position, because it entails neglecting other prohibitions revealed after it in the Qur'an, and neglecting what is authentically related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said after the revelation of this verse, without any cause requiring that or any ground obliging it. As for Jabir's saying, "But that sea, Ibn 'Abbas, refused it," in the narration of al-Bukhari mentioned above, I say: even if that sea refused it, it is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Holding to the saying of a Companion against the saying of the Prophet ﷺ is poor judgment and lack of fairness. End of the words of Fath.

In Nayl al-Awtar: Deriving evidence from this verse is only valid regarding things for which no text of prohibition has been transmitted. As for domestic donkeys, the texts on their prohibition are mutawatir, and explicit prohibition takes precedence over the generality of permission, and over analogy. Also, the verse is Meccan. End quote.

It is established from Ibn 'Umar that he retracted from relying on its generality.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Imam Ahmad, and Abu Dawud related from Numaylah al-Fazzazi who said: "I was (p-2537) with Ibn 'Umar, when he was asked about eating the hedgehog, so he recited to him: "Say: I do not find..." the verse. An elderly man present said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: It was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "It is one of the most vile of vile things." Ibn 'Umar said: If the Prophet ﷺ said it, then it is as he said."

That is: vile things are forbidden by the explicit text of the Qur'an, so this specifies the generality of this verse.

From al-Miqdam ibn Ma'di Karib who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Is there not a man who will receive a hadith from me while reclining on his couch, and he will say: Between us and you is the Book of Allah. What we find in it as lawful we make lawful, and what we find in it as unlawful we make unlawful. Indeed, what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade is like what Allah, Exalted is He, forbade." Related by al-Tirmidhi, who said: a hasan gharib hadith.

And for Abu Dawud, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I have been given the Book and its like with it. Soon a man full and reclining on his couch will say: Hold to this Qur'an; what you find in it of lawful, make lawful, and what you find in it of unlawful, make unlawful. Surely it is not lawful for you (the flesh of) the domestic donkey, nor every animal with fangs among predators, nor the lost property of a covenanted non-Muslim unless its owner has no need of it. Whoever alights among a people, it is incumbent upon them to host him. If they do not host him, he may take from them compensation equal to his hospitality." (That is: he takes from them a recompense for what they withheld of hospitality.)

Furthermore, al-Zamakhshari interpreted ﹛muharram﹜ as "forbidden food among the foods which you have forbidden," and made the exception disjunctive (munqati'), meaning: I do not find what you have forbidden, but I find the four forbidden. This has no indication of restriction (hasr) so as to require the other prohibitions, since a disjunctive exception does not carry the force of restriction as a conjunctive one does. Other than al-Zamakhshari did not restrict it to what was mentioned, because the original state is connection and absence of restriction, and they interpreted it according to what we mentioned before. In that case the exception is from the most general of times or the most general of states, with a restricted (mufarragh) construction, meaning: I do not find (p-2538) any of the forbidden foods at any time or in any state, except at a time or state in which the food is one of the four; then I do find something forbidden at that time. So the infinitive is for time or manner. And in this there is the point that the infinitive construction of "an" and the verb cannot be put in the accusative as an adverb of time, nor can it serve as a circumstantial accusative, since it is definite. And Allah knows best.

The second: In His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden"﴾ is an indication that the determination of prohibition is only through revelation, not through whim. Al-Shihab said: He expressed non-finding as a metaphor for non-existence. The basis of this metaphor is that the way of prohibition is explicit stipulation from Him, Exalted is He. And they affirmed interpreting it as revelation in general. For this reason He said "revealed" and did not say "sent down."

The third: As-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: The Prophet ﷺ derived evidence from His saying ﴿on an eater who would eat it﴾ that only the eating of carrion is forbidden, and that its hide becomes pure by tanning. Ahmad and others related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "A sheep belonging to Sawdah bint Zam'ah died, so she said: O Messenger of Allah! So-and-so died (meaning the sheep). He said: Why did you not take its hide? She said: Shall we take the hide of a sheep that has died? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only said: ﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, except that it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine﴾—for you do not eat it. If you tan it, you may benefit from it." So she sent for it, flayed its hide, tanned it, made a water-skin from it, until it wore out in her possession."

The fourth: It was deduced from His saying, Exalted is He, "poured forth" (masfuhan) the permissibility of what is other than it. That is because blood poured forth is what flows from the animal while alive or at slaughter, not like the liver and spleen; and likewise blood mixed into the flesh, since it is not flowing. Imran ibn Jadir said: I asked Abu Mijlaz about blood mixed into the meat, and about a cooking pot in which the redness of blood is seen. He said: There is no harm in that! It is only blood poured forth that was forbidden.

(p-2539) Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: There is no harm in blood in a vein or in marrow, except what is poured forth.

And 'Ikrimah said: Were it not for this verse, the Muslims would pursue blood from the veins as the Jews pursued it.

Then He, exalted is He, made clear that He had also forbidden the Jews other things besides these four, to expose the fabrications of the polytheists regarding what they had forbidden, since none of it agreed with anything that God had sent down. So He, glorified is He, said:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of the words of God, exalted is He:

[146] ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws. And of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry, or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That was Our recompense to them for their rebellion. And indeed, We are truthful.﴾

﴿And to those who were Jews﴾, that is, the Jews specifically: ﴿We forbade every animal with claws﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is that which does not have split toes, such as the camel, the hyrax (al-wabr) and the rabbit, for these have claws that are not cloven, that is, not divided. As for the animal with cloven claws that chews the cud among the beasts, it was not forbidden to them.

﴿And of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat﴾, not their flesh (lahum, "لا لُحُومَهُما" is not the reading, rather the fat is what is forbidden): ﴿except what their backs carry﴾, meaning what clings to the back of fat; ﴿or the entrails﴾, that is, the intestines and the viscera (al-maṣārīn), meaning the fat they carry; ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾, such as the marrow and the coccyx (al-'u'su'ṣ). ﴿That﴾, that is, the forbidding of those good things to them, ﴿was Our recompense to them for their rebellion﴾, because of their wrongdoing, which was their killing of the prophets without right, their consuming of usury (ribā), though they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of people's wealth falsely. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them, and for their hindering many from the way of God﴾ [al-Nisa: 160].

Al-Mahayimi said: that is, that rebellion was not found in others, so there is no basis for forbidding these things to them, given that they are good in themselves.

﴿And indeed, We are truthful﴾, that is, in all Our reports, of which this report is one; namely, restricting the prohibition to them because of their rebellion. (p-2540) Ibn Jarir said: not as they claimed, that Israel was the one who forbade it upon himself.

Abu al-Su'ud said: His saying, exalted is He, has indeed silenced them: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel forbade upon himself before the Torah was revealed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93]. ﴿Say: Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93].

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[147] ﴿And if they deny you, say: "Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy, and His punishment is not averted from the guilty people."﴾

﴿And if they deny you﴾: the pronoun may refer to the Jews, because they are the nearest in mention, and because the polytheists are mentioned afterward under the title of polytheism; or it may refer to the polytheists; or to both groups. That is: if the Jews deny you concerning the specification, and claim that Allah's prohibition is not abrogated, and insist on the claim of the antiquity of the prohibition; or the polytheists deny you concerning what has been detailed of the rulings on what is lawful and what is forbidden; or both deny you concerning what they claim. ﴿Then say: "Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy"﴾, who gives you respite in your denial, so do not be deceived by His respite, for He does not neglect: ﴿and His punishment is not averted from the guilty people﴾. That is: and along with His mercy, He is of severe punishment. In this is an encouragement for them to seek the vast mercy of Allah, which lies in following His good pleasure, and a warning against opposition.

It should be known that when the polytheists were bound by the proof, through the invalidity of what they held of associating others with Allah and forbidding what Allah had not forbidden, Allah, Exalted is He, informed about them of what they would say of doubt to which they cling for their polytheism and their prohibition of what they had prohibited. The benefit of informing of what they will say is to settle the soul upon the answer, to confront them with refutation, and to prepare the proof before its time. Thus Allah, Exalted is He, said:

(p-2541) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[148] ﴿The idolaters will say: "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything." Likewise did those before them deny, until they tasted Our might. Say: "Have you any knowledge that you can bring forth for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess."﴾

﴿The idolaters will say﴾ meaning the idolaters of Quraysh and the Arabs. ﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything﴾ meaning what they prohibited of the baheera (she-camel slit-eared and released), the sa'iba (animal set free), and others. ﴿Likewise did those before them deny, until they tasted Our might﴾ that is, until We sent down punishment upon them. ﴿Say: "Have you any knowledge that you can bring forth for us?"﴾ that is, a certain matter that is valid as evidence for what you claim, so that you may show it to us. ﴿You follow nothing but conjecture﴾ that is, regarding what you are upon of polytheism and the prohibition of what you have prohibited. ﴿And you do nothing but guess﴾ that is, you lie.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[149] ﴿Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof. Had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾

﴿Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof"﴾: *al-bayyinah al-wadihah* (the clear evidence) that has reached the utmost firmness and strength in establishing the claim. From this usage comes *ayman balighah* (emphatic oaths), meaning strongly affirmed oaths. Or *al-balighah* means the proof by which its holder has established the soundness of his claim, as in *ʿIshatin radiyah* (a pleasing life). ﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾: that is, but He did not will that. Rather, He willed the guidance of some who directed their choice toward following the path of truth, and the misguidance of others who directed their acquisition toward the opposite, without any compeller turning them or any inclination bending them. So this happened in the manner He willed.

The Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi said in his *Ta'wilat*: It was said that the verse concerns the polytheists of the Arabs. They said this when they were confronted with contradiction and their argument failed regarding the prohibition of certain things they had forbidden. They attributed this [to God], and it is the continuation of His saying: ﴿eight pairs﴾ [al-An'am: 143], up to His saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you?﴾ [al-An'am: 144]. When contradiction befell them and their argument failed, they resorted to this statement: "Had God willed, we would not have associated [others with Him]." End of quotation.

The purpose is to excuse everything they undertook of associating partners [with God] and forbidding what is lawful. That is, He did not will them to abandon it, but willed their action; so our action is subject to His will, and He wills only the truth, since He is capable. Had it not been truth that He approves of, He would have prevented us from it. He did not prevent us, so it is truth. In relating this debate and dispute there is a clarification of a kind of their disbelief which is extremely abominable!

*Tanbih* (a note):
This verse has parallels repeated in the Noble Revelation in several surahs, and it is among the verses deserving of reflection in order to sift out the truth regarding its intended meaning.

The Mu'tazilah claimed that it contains a clear proof for their doctrine that God does not will sins and disbelief, as al-Tabarsi the Shi'i boasted in his *Tafsir* and said that it contains a clear refutation of whoever attributes the willing of that to God, the Glorified; and likewise al-Zamakhshari in his *Tafsir*.

It is well known that the creed of the saved sect (*al-firqah al-najiyah*) is belief that: whatever God wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be; that there is no movement or stillness in the heavens and the earth except by the will of God, the Glorified; nothing occurs in His dominion except what He wills; and He is the Creator of the acts of His servants.

Most of the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree over human acts) disagreed on this, and the Prophet ﷺ called them the Magians of this Ummah. They said: there is no will except in the sense of volition, and He wills only what He commanded, and He did not create any of the acts of the servants. So in their view most of what occurs of the acts of the servants happens contrary to His will, exalted is He. Since their statement is extremely abominable, the Companions disavowed them. The root of their innovation, as Ibn Taymiyyah said, was the incapacity of their minds to believe in God's decree while also believing in His command and prohibition. We will clarify the verification of that after we set forth their doubt regarding this verse and refute it, with His help, the Exalted, by several aspects. So we say:

They said: God, the Exalted, related of the polytheists that they said: "We associated [others with God] by the will of God, the Exalted. Had He willed our not associating, we would not have associated, and the prohibition of the lawful things would not have come from us." Thus they ascribed their disbelief and disobedience to His will, the Exalted, just as you claim. Then He, the Exalted, refuted their statement, clarified its falsehood, blamed them for it, and threatened them for it with a severe threat. So if it were permissible to attribute will to God, the Exalted, in that, as you attribute, would He not have refuted them and threatened them?

We say: The will in the verse can be interpreted in several ways:

First: What al-Hasan and al-Asamm said: the will here means approval. So their meaning is: God approved of our act and deed, since our forefathers did what we did, so God did not stand between them and that, nor did He take them by the hand, nor did He prevent them from it. Had He not approved of it, He would have prevented them from it!

Abu Mansur said: They only inferred approval and permission from God regarding what they were engaged in because they were threatened with destruction and punishment for their conduct, then they saw their forefathers died upon it and punishment did not come to them. So they inferred from the delay of the descent of punishment upon them that God approved of that.

In sum, by their statement they meant that they were upon the lawful truth that is approved by God. But since their argument was refuted and false, because if it had been sound God would not have made them taste His might, would not have destroyed them, and would not have given His noble messengers power over them, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can bring forth to us?"﴾ [al-An'am: 148], that is: that God is pleased with you in what you are engaged in! This is mockery and testimony that such a statement could never have a valid proof.

In *al-Wajiz*: The outcome is that the polytheists believed there is no distinction between what is commanded and approved and what is willed, just as the Mu'tazilah believed, so they argued for the rightness of associating [others with God]. What indicates this is His saying: ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾, for if the meaning were that this is not by God's will, He would have said (*kadhalika kadhaba*) with the light form rather than the intensive form. This verse, to one who has an attentive ear, cries out against the Mu'tazilah with woe and perdition, but there is deafness in their ears, and whom God does not guide, none can guide. End of quotation.

Second: The will in the verse means command and calling to that. That is, they say: God commanded them to it and called them to it, as He related of them in Surah al-A'raf in His saying: ﴿When they commit an indecency they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and God commanded us to it."﴾ [al-A'raf: 28]. God replied to them with His saying: ﴿Say: "Indeed, God does not command indecency."﴾ [al-A'raf: 28].

Third: Their statement was by way of mockery and derision, repelling his ﷺ call and pretending as an excuse for not responding to and submitting to him, not as a delegation of created beings to the will of God, the Exalted. So nothing proceeded from them but a word of truth by which falsehood was intended. For this reason God blamed them with denial (*al-takdhib*): they intended by it to deny the Prophet ﷺ regarding the obligation to follow him and comply with him. So He said: ﴿Thus did they deny﴾ with the intensive form, and He did not blame them for lying in their statement, for otherwise He would have said (*kadhalika kadhaba*) with the light form, indicating that the statement in itself is true and sincere.

Another said: ﴿Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof. Had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ He thereby pointed to the truth of their statement and the corruption of their aim. So the rebuke that befell them and the threat He made against them was only because of their mockery.

(p-٢٥٤٥) As mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And man says, "When I am dead, shall I indeed be brought out alive?"﴾ [Maryam: 66]. It is a word of truth, but he said it in mockery, so he incurred blame.

Al-ʿAḍud (al-Ijī) in *al-Mawaqif* restricted himself to this aspect, and al-Maturidi also established it in his *Ta'wilat*.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fudayl said: Had they said this statement out of glorifying God, reverencing Him, knowing His right and what they were saying, He would not have reproached them for it. But they said this statement in denial and disputation, without knowledge of God and of what they were saying.

Fourth: What is derived from the words of the Imam: In the speech of the polytheists there are two premises:
One: that disbelief is by the will of God, the Exalted.
The second: that it follows from it that the call of the Prophet ﷺ is void. The blame and reproach that came only concern the second premise, since God does what He wills and decides what He intends. He may will disbelief from the unbeliever, command him to believe, punish him for opposing it, and send the prophets, upon them be blessings and peace, as callers to the Abode of Peace, even though He guides only whom He wills.

Fifth: Their statement was by way of obstinacy and arrogance.

Al-Biqaʿi said regarding His saying: ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾ [al-An'am: 148], that is: by what they produced of this kind of dispute in their saying: if everything is by God's will, then obligation is futile, and the claims of the prophets are void.
