This statement from the polytheists is obstinacy after the establishment of the messages by miracles and the messengers' report that He wills a thing and punishes for it, because His dominion is complete, and He is not questioned about what He does.

Al-Imam al-Qashani, may God sanctify his secret, said regarding His saying: ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾ [al-An'am: 148], that is: the deniers denied the messengers before them by making their disbelief conditional upon God's will, out of obstinacy and arrogance, so they were punished for their disbelief.

Then he said regarding His saying: ﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can bring forth to us?"﴾ [al-An'am: 148], that is: if you have (p-٢٥٤٦) knowledge of that and proof, then state it. He only said this to point to their saying: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated [others with Him]﴾ [al-An'am: 148], because if they had said that from knowledge, they would have known that the faith of the monotheists and everything else occurs only by the will of God. Then they would not have opposed them or denied them, but would have allied with them, and no disagreement would remain between them and the believers. By my life, if they had said that from knowledge, they would not have been polytheists but monotheists! But they followed conjecture in that, and built upon speculation and guesswork for the purpose of denial and obstinacy, and upon what they heard from the messengers as a means of holding them to account and establishing that they did not refrain from the messengers, because they are veiled in the station of the self. How could they have certainty? From where could they have insight into God's will?

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof"﴾, that is: if your supposition is true that your polytheism is conditioned on God's will, then you have no proof against the believers or against others of the religions, because on that basis every religion is by God's will, so you must agree with them and affirm them. Rather, the conclusive proof belongs to God against you regarding the obligation to affirm them and your acknowledgment that you associated [others with Him], with One for whom nothing occurs except by His will, for what has no effect of His will at all. So you are wretched from eternity, deserving of distance and punishment.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾, that is: Yes, you have spoken truly. But just as He willed your disbelief, had He willed, He would have guided you all. So by what did you know that He did not will your guidance, such that you persisted? This is an incitement for whoever among them might have a readiness, so that he might restrain himself, be guided, turn back from polytheism, and believe. End of quotation.

Sixth: What is in *Lubab al-Ta'wil*, that it was said regarding the meaning of the verse: they used to speak the truth with this phrase, which is their saying: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated [others with Him]﴾ [al-An'am: 148], except that they regarded it as an excuse for themselves and made it an argument for them in abandoning faith. The response to them in this is that God's command is separate from His will and volition. For God, the Exalted, wills all beings without commanding all that He wills. So the servant must follow His command and may not cling to His will, for His will is not an excuse for anyone regarding his act. He, the Exalted, wills disbelief from the unbeliever without approving of it or commanding it; yet despite this, He sends messengers to the servant and commands him to believe. The occurrence of a command contrary to the will is not impossible. The outcome is that (p-٢٥٤٧) He, the Exalted, related of the unbelievers that they cling to God's will for their polytheism and disbelief, and God, the Exalted, informed that this clinging is corrupt and false, for the will of God in all matters does not entail the repelling of the call of the prophets, peace be upon them. End of quotation.

The seventh aspect is what al-Nasir (Ibn al-Munayyir) established in *al-Intisaf*: the refutation was directed at them because they believed that they were stripped of their choice and power, that their association of partners with Allah (shirk) proceeded from them under compulsion, and that they claimed to establish proof against Allah and His messengers by this. So Allah rejected their claim and their lie in their assertion that they had no choice of their own. He likened them to those who were deceived by this same illusion before them, so they denied the messengers and associated partners with Allah, relying on the idea that all of this happens only by the will of Allah, and they aimed to confound the messengers with this doubt. Then Allah Most High made clear that they have no proof in this, and that the conclusive proof belongs to Him, not to them, by His saying: ﴿Then to Allah belongs the conclusive argument﴾. Then Most High clarified that everything that occurs does so by His will, and that He willed from them only what proceeded from them. And that if He had willed their guidance, they would all have been guided, by His saying: ﴿...if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾.

The purpose of this is that the aspect of refutation directed at them be made pure, and that the belief in the execution of the divine will and the generality of its connection to every existent be freed from the refutation. The refutation thus applies to their claim of depriving themselves of choice, and to their establishing proof by that claim specifically. When you reflect on this, you will find it sufficient to refute whoever among the people of the qibla (ahl al-qibla, the Muslims) claims that the servant has no choice or power whatsoever, but is entirely compelled in his actions and forced to perform them. These are the sect known as the Mujbirah (the Determinists, or Compulsionists). Al-Zamakhshari misrepresents realities by calling the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah, the Sunni community) "Mujbirah," even though they affirm choice and power for the servant. This is because they negate the causal effect of the servant's power and hold that it accompanies his voluntary acts, distinguishing between those and his compelled acts. From this angle he equated them with the Mujbirah and made it a general label for Ahl al-Sunnah. By consensus, the refutation in the words of Allah Most High ﴿Those who associated partners will say...﴾ [al-An'am 6:148], up to His saying ﴿Say: Then to Allah belongs the conclusive argument﴾, is directed at the Mujbirah, whom we have distinguished from Ahl al-Sunnah. The rest of the verse is an explicit refutation of the "sect of the Mu'tazilah" (ta'ifat al-I'tizal), who say that Allah Most High willed the guidance of all of them. But it did not come to pass for most of them!

The method of refutation is this: when the particle "law" (lau, "if") enters upon an affirmative verb, it negates it. This entails that when Allah Most High said "if He had willed," the actual situation is that He did not will their guidance. Had He willed it, it would have occurred. This is an explicit statement of the falsity of their claim and of the foundation of their doctrine.

Once it is established that the verse includes a refutation of the beliefs of the two mentioned groups, the Mujbirah at its beginning and the Mu'tazilah at its end, know that it encompasses the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah and corresponds to it. Its beginning, as we have explained, affirms choice and power for the servant in a way that cuts off his argument and his excuse for opposition and disobedience. Its end affirms Allah's dominion over the servant, and that all his actions are in accordance with the divine will, whether good or otherwise. This is precisely the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah. For they, just as they affirm will and power for the servant, negate their causal effect, and they believe that their affirmation is decisive against his argument and obligates him to obedience in accordance with his choice. They also affirm the will and power of Allah over the actions of His servants. Thus they, as you have seen, follow the Mighty Book: they affirm what it affirms and negate what it negates, supported by reason and by transmission. And Allah is the Granter of success. End of quotation.

Al-Hakim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it was said to him: "Some people say: evil is not by qadar (divine decree)." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Between us and the People of Qadar (al-Qadariyyah, those who deny divine decree) is this verse: ﴿Those who associated partners will say...﴾ [al-An'am 6:148], up to His saying: ﴿...then if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾."

By verifying these aspects, the statement of al-Tabarsi the Mu'tazili falls away. He said: "If the matter were as the people of compulsion (ahl al-jabr) say, that Allah Most High willed disbelief from them, then the disbelievers would have a proof against Allah, since they did what Allah willed, and they would thereby be obedient to Him, because obedience is carrying out the command that is intended. Nor would there be a proof for Allah against them on their view, since He created disbelief in them and willed it from them. So what proof would He have against them in that case?" End of quotation.

Likewise is the statement of al-Zamakhshari: what is related about the polytheists is exactly the doctrine of the Mujbirah. For this reason al-Nihrir said: "Yes! It is like their doctrine that every existent occurs by the will of Allah. But the disbelievers use this as an argument for the truth of their association of partners, the prohibition of what is lawful, and all the other abominations they commit. And their deeds are not sinful, because they conform to the will, which is equivalent to the meaning of the command, according to the doctrine of the Qadariyyah, who make no distinction between what is commanded and what is willed, and hold that whatever Allah wills is not a sin prohibited by Him." The Mujbirah believe that everything occurs by the will of Allah, yet they believe that association of partners and all the abominations are acts of disobedience and violations of the command, for which punishment is incurred according to the threat (wa'id), while He pardons some of them according to the promise (wa'd). In this they affirm what reason and revelation indicate, namely that it is impossible for most of what occurs in His dominion to be contrary to what He wills. The disbelievers, however, deny that the threat applies to what occurs by His Most High will. End of quotation.

**Chapter**

The Imam Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim al-Dimashqi, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book *Tariq al-Hijratayn* (*The Path of the Two Migrations*), after lengthily enumerating the hadiths and reports about qadar, the following:

The answer is that there are two stations here: a station of faith, guidance and salvation, and a station of error, perdition and destruction, in which feet have slipped and carried their owners down to the abode of misery.

As for the station of faith, guidance and salvation, it is the station of affirming qadar and believing in it, and attributing all existent things to the will of their Lord, their Creator and Originator, and that what He wills comes to be even if people do not will it, and what He does not will does not come to be, even if people will it. These reports, all of which establish this station, show that whoever does not believe in qadar has stripped himself of monotheism (tawhid) and put on the garment of shirk. Indeed, he has not believed in Allah and has not known Him. This holds in every Book that Allah sent down to His messengers.

As for the second station, the station of error, perdition and destruction, it is to use qadar as an argument against Allah, to place one's sin upon one's Lord, and to absolve one's ignorant, wrongdoing, commanding-to-evil soul, to the extent that one of these people says:

*He threw him into the river bound, and said to him: "Beware, beware of getting wet with water!"*

And another of them says:

*He called me and shut the door behind me. Is there a way for me to enter? Tell me my story!*

Then he (may Allah have mercy on him) related strange stories about this. Then he said:

I heard him, meaning Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, say: "The Qadariyyah who are censured in the Sunnah and by the words of the Salaf are these three groups: the deniers of qadar, who are the 'Majusi Qadariyyah' (Magian Qadariyyah). Those who oppose the Sharia with it, who say: 'If Allah had willed, we would not have associated partners,' and they are the 'Mushriki Qadariyyah' (polytheistic Qadariyyah). And those who dispute with the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, by it; they are the enemies and adversaries of Allah, the 'Iblisi Qadariyyah' (Satanic Qadariyyah), whose shaykh is Iblis. He was the first to argue against Allah with qadar, saying: 'Because You have led me astray' (Qur'an 7:16). He did not acknowledge the sin and bear its burden as Adam did. Whoever acknowledges the sin, bears it, and declares his Lord free of wrong, resembles his father Adam, and whoever resembles his father has not wronged. Whoever clears himself and argues against his Lord with qadar resembles Iblis. There is no doubt that these Iblisi and polytheistic Qadariyyah are worse than the negating Qadariyyah, because the negators only negated it to exalt the Lord and to glorify Him against decreeing sin and then blaming and punishing for it. They declared Him free of punishing the servant for what the servant had no part in at all. Rather, it is like his height, his shortness, his blackness, his whiteness, and the like. As is related of one of the Jabriyyah: he attended the assembly of one of the rulers, and a pickpocket (tarrar, the one who cuts the sleeves or pockets and takes what is in them) with a squint was brought in. The ruler said to him: 'What do you think of him?' He said: 'Beat him fifteen,' meaning fifteen lashes. One of those present, one of those who deny compulsion, said: 'Rather, he should be beaten thirty lashes: fifteen for his pickpocketing and the same for his squint.' The Jabri said: 'How can he be beaten for the squint when he has no part in it?' He replied: 'Just as he is beaten for the pickpocketing, in which he has no part according to you.' The Jabri was silenced."

As for the "Iblisi and polytheistic Qadariyyah," many of them have stripped themselves of the Sharia, are enemies of Allah and His Messenger, and acknowledge neither command nor prohibition. This is an inheritance from their shaykhs, about whom Allah said: ﴿Those who associated partners will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated partners, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything."﴾ [al-An'am 6:148]. He also said Most High: ﴿Those who associated partners said: "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything other than Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything other than Him." Likewise did those before them do. But upon the messengers is only the clear delivery.﴾ [al-Nahl 16:35]. And He said Most High: ﴿They said: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:20]. And He said: ﴿When it is said to them: "Spend from what Allah has provided you," those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Shall we feed one whom Allah, if He willed, would feed? You are only in clear error."﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:47]. These are four places in the Qur'an in which He, glorified be He, made clear that using qadar as an argument is the act of polytheists who deny the messengers.

People have differed in their interpretation of these verses into four groups:

The first group considered this argument a valid argument, and that the one who argues with it has a proof against Allah. This group then split into two sects. One sect denied the command, the promise and the threat, and claimed that after this, command, prohibition, promise and threat would be injustice, and Allah does not wrong any of His creatures! The other sect affirmed the command, prohibition, promise and threat, and said: "That is not injustice. Allah disposes of His dominion as He wills, and punishes the servant for what he had no part in; rather, He punishes him for His own act, not for the act of His servant, since the servant's act belongs to Him, the dominion is His, and He is not questioned about what He does, but they are questioned." These disbelievers made this statement, which Allah related about them, in mockery. Had they said it out of conviction in the decree and qadar, and in attributing all existent things to His will and power, it would not have been rejected of them. The implication of this group's view is that this is a valid argument if they say it as a belief, not in mockery, so the polytheists would have a proof against Allah. And that suffices to show its corruption and invalidity.

The second group took these verses as an argument for them to invalidate the decree, the qadar and the general will. For if the general will were sound, and Allah had willed from them shirk, disbelief and the worship of idols, they would have spoken the truth, and Allah would have confirmed them in it and not rejected it of them. But since He described it as conjecture (kharṣ), which is falsehood, and denied them knowledge, this indicates that what they said is not correct, and that they were lying in it. For had it been knowledge, they would have been truthful in reporting it, and He would not have said to them: "Do you have any knowledge?"

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 149 (part 3 of 4):

This group made these verses a proof for themselves in denying qada' and qadar (divine decree and predestination), and they claimed by them that there exists in His dominion what He does not will, and that He wills what does not come to be, and that He has no power over the actions of His servants, whether men, jinn or angels, nor over the actions of animals. They said that He cannot cause anyone to go astray, nor guide him, nor grant him more success than He has already given him, nor protect him from sins and disbelief, nor inspire him with his right guidance, nor place faith in his heart, nor is He the One who made the one who prays a praying person, the righteous one righteous, the wicked one wicked, the believer a believer, or the disbeliever a disbeliever. Rather, they themselves made themselves such.

This group shared with the group before it in kindling the war and enmity between the Shari'ah and qadar. The first group inclined toward qadar and waged war against the Shari'ah; the second inclined toward the Shari'ah and denied qadar. Both groups are astray, and one of them is more astray than the other.

As for the third group: they believed in qada' and qadar and affirmed the command and the prohibition. They placed each thing in its proper station: qada' and qadar are to be believed in but not used as an argument, while the command and the prohibition are to be carried out and obeyed. Thus, in their view, belief in qada' and qadar is part of the completeness of tawhid and of the testimony that there is no god but Allah. And upholding the command and the prohibition is the requirement of the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. They said: whoever does not affirm qada' and qadar, and does not uphold the command and the prohibition, has denied both testimonies, even if he utters them with his tongue. Then they split into two groups regarding the meaning of these verses:

(One group) said: what was rejected in them was only their using the general will and qada' and qadar as proof for His approval and love of that. They made His will for it and His decree for it a proof of His pleasure with it and His love for it, for if He had hated it and detested it, He would have prevented it from them. For the wise one, when he is able to repel what he hates and detests, he repels it and prevents it from occurring. And if He did not prevent its occurrence, it would necessarily follow either that He lacks power or that He lacks wisdom, and both are impossible with respect to Allah. Thus it is known that He loves what we are upon of worshipping other than Him and of associating partners with Him.

Some who agreed with these people said: Allah loves disbelief, wickedness and disobedience and is pleased with them. But they differed with them in that He forbade them, commanded the opposites of them, and punishes for them; so they agreed with them on half of their statement and disagreed on the other half.

These verses are among the greatest proofs against the views of both groups, and that the will of Allah the Exalted, His decree and His qadar do not necessitate His love and approval of everything He wills and decrees.

As for these polytheists, when they used His will as evidence for His love and approval, He refuted them and rejected their claim, informing that they have no knowledge of that, and that they are liars and fabricators. For Allah's love for a thing and His approval of it are known only through His command concerning it, conveyed by the tongue of His Messenger, not merely by His creating it. He created Iblis and his hosts, who are His enemies, and He, glorified is He, hates them and curses them, yet they are His creation. So it is with actions: He created their good and their evil, and He loves their good, commands it, and rewards for it; and He hates their evil, forbids it, and punishes for it. Both are His creation. To Allah belongs the perfect, complete, far-reaching wisdom in creating what He hates and detests, of essences, attributes and actions, each proceeding from His wisdom and knowledge, just as it proceeds from His power and will.

The second group said: what was rejected in them was only their opposing the Shari'ah with qadar, and their repelling the command with the will. So when the proof of Allah was established against them and His command and prohibition bound them, they repelled it with His decree and qadar. They made qada' and qadar (p-2554) into a nullification of the call of the Messengers and a repelling of what they brought. Their brothers and descendants shared in this with them, those who argue with qada' and qadar for sins and transgressions in half of their statement, and disagreed with them on the other half, which is their affirmation of the command and the prohibition.

Observe how these inheritances were divided among these shares, and how every people inherited its leaders and forebears, either in all of their legacy, or in much of it, or in a part of it. Allah, by His grace, guided the heirs of His prophets and messengers to the inheritance of their Prophet and his companions, so they did not believe in some of the Book and disbelieve in some of it, but believed in the decree of Allah, His qadar and His general, binding will, and that whatever Allah wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be, and that He is the Turner of hearts and their Director however He wishes, and that He is the One who made the believer a believer, the praying one a praying one, and the God-fearing one God-fearing, and made the leaders of guidance guide by His command, and the leaders of misguidance call to the Fire; and that He inspired every soul with its wickedness and its piety; and that He guides whom He wills by His justice and wisdom; and that He is the One who granted success to the people of obedience to obey Him, so they obeyed Him, and had He willed, He would have forsaken them, so they would have disobeyed Him; and that He comes between the disbelievers and their hearts, for He comes between a person and his heart, so they disbelieved in Him, and had He willed, He would have granted them success, so they would have believed in Him and obeyed Him; and that whomever Allah guides, there is no misleader for him, and whomever He misguides, there is no guide for him; and that had He willed, they would not have fought one another, but Allah does what He wills; and that had your Lord willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.

The qada' and qadar, according to them, are four levels, which their Prophet brought and reported from his Lord, the Exalted:

The first: His prior knowledge of what they will do before bringing them into existence.

The second: the writing of that in the Reminder (al-Dhikr) with Him before the creation of the heavens and the earth.

The third: His will, which encompasses every existent thing, so nothing in existence goes outside His will, just as nothing goes outside His knowledge.

The fourth: His creating it, bringing it into being and originating it, for there is no creator except Allah, and Allah is the creator of everything.

So the Creator, according to them, is one, and whatever is other than Him is created. There is no intermediary, according to them, between the Creator and the created. And they believe, together with this, in His wisdom, and that He is wise in everything He does and creates, and that the source of all of that is a perfect wisdom, which is what necessitated its proceeding and its creation. And that His wisdom is a true wisdom, returning to Him and subsisting in Him, like His other attributes, and it is not an expression for the correspondence of His knowledge to its object of knowledge and His power to its object of power, as the deniers of wisdom say, who affirm its word but not its reality. Rather, it is a matter beyond that: it is the beloved and sought end for Him, which is the object of His love and praise, and for the sake of which He created, proportioned, decreed and guided, caused to die and to live, made wretched and misguided and guided, withheld and gave. This wisdom is the end, and the act is the means to it. So affirming the act while negating it is affirming the means and negating the ends, which is impossible, since negating the end necessitates negating the means. Thus negating the means, which is the act, necessarily follows from negating the end, which is wisdom. And negating that the act and wisdom subsist in their agent is in reality negating both; for an act that does not subsist in its doer, and a wisdom that does not subsist in the wise one, is something unintelligible. And that necessitates denying His lordship and His divinity. This is a necessary consequence for whoever negates that, and he cannot escape it, even if he refuses to accept it. As for whoever affirms His wisdom and His acts in the manner that accords with reason and innate nature and what the Messengers brought, no forbidden consequence follows from his statement at all; rather his statement is true, and the necessary consequence of the truth is true, whatever it may be. The point is: the heirs of the Messengers and their successors, owing to the completeness of their inheritance from their Prophet, believed in the qada' and qadar, the wisdoms and the defined ends in the acts and commands of the Lord; and they upheld, together with that, the command and the prohibition, and affirmed the promise. Thus they believed in the creation, the completeness of whose belief includes affirming qadar and wisdom; and in the command, the completeness of whose belief includes belief in the promise and threat, the resurrection of bodies, and reward and punishment. So they affirmed the creation and the command, and did not negate them by negating their necessary consequences, as the Magian Qadariyya and the Qadariyya who oppose the command with qadar did. They were the happiest of people with the creation and the closest in lineage to this prophetic inheritance. And: "That is the grace of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Owner of mighty grace."

Know that belief in the reality of qadar, the Shari'ah and wisdom is not gathered except in the hearts of the elite of creation (p-2556) and the intellect of the scholar. The matter is not in believing in the words of these designations while denying their realities, as many sects of the misguided do. For the Qadariyya believe in the word "qadar," and some of them reduce it to knowledge, and some reduce it to the religious command, making His decree and qadar the very same as His command and prohibition and the very same as the will of Allah for the acts of His servants by His commanding them with them; and this is the reality of denying qada' and qadar. Likewise "wisdom": the Jabriyya believe in its word and deny its reality, for they make it the correspondence of Allah's knowledge to its object of knowledge and His will to its object of will, so it is, according to them, the occurrence of beings in accordance with His knowledge and will. The Qadariyya deniers are not content with this; rather they rise above it by a level and affirm a wisdom additional to that, but they deny its subsisting in the wise Agent, and they make it a created thing among His creations, as they said about His speech and His will. All of these have affirmed the word "wisdom" and denied its meaning and reality. Likewise "command" and "Shari'ah": whoever denies the speech of Allah and says that Allah has not spoken and does not speak, has not said and does not say, does not love anything and does not hate anything, and all existing things are beloved to Him, and what does not exist is hateful to Him, and He does not love, is not pleased, and does not become angry, and there is no difference in reality between truthfulness and lying, wickedness and prostration to idols, the sun and the moon. Without doubt this removes the Shari'ahs and the command and prohibition altogether. Were it not for the contradiction of those who say it, they would have stripped themselves of the religion of the Messengers; but the situation continued somewhat through their contradiction, and that is better for them than discarding their principles and holding to their necessary implications.

The point is: no one believed in qada' and qadar, wisdom, command and prohibition, promise and threat, in their true reality, except the followers of the Messengers and their heirs.

The qada' and qadar originate from the knowledge and power of the Lord. For this reason Imam Ahmad said: "Qadar is the power of Allah." Ibn 'Aqil highly praised this statement of Ahmad, saying: "He healed with this word and clarified the reality of qadar by it."

For this reason, the deniers of qadar were of two groups: one group denied the prior knowledge and rejected it, and these are their extremists (p-2557) whom the early generations and the imams declared disbelievers, and from whom the Companions disassociated themselves. And another group denied the completeness of power, and rejected that the acts of the servants are within Allah's power, and explicitly stated that Allah has no power over them. Thus these denied the Lord's power, and the other denied His complete knowledge. The Jabriyya opposed them: they came with affirming power and knowledge, and denied wisdom and mercy.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 149 (part 4 of 4):

Therefore the source of creation, command, decree and legislation lies in the knowledge, might and wisdom of the Lord. For this reason, Exalted is He, He often pairs these three names and attributes, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from the presence of One Wise, All-Knowing﴾ [An-Naml: 6], and His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing﴾ [Ghafir: 2], and His saying: ﴿Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [Al-Jathiya: 1-2]. He also said, in (Ha-Mim Fussilat, after mentioning the creation of the world): ﴿That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing﴾. He mentioned a similar statement in (Al-An'am), saying: ﴿He is the Splitter of the dawn, and He has made the night for rest and the sun and moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing﴾ [Al-An'am: 96]. So the connection of creation to His perfect power requires that no existing thing escapes His power. Its connection to His perfect knowledge requires that He encompasses it and precedes it. Its connection to His wisdom requires that it occurs in the most complete and best of forms, and that it includes the praiseworthy end that is sought by the Lord, glorified is He. Likewise, His command is (issued) with His knowledge, wisdom and might. So He is All-Knowing of His creation and His command, and Wise in His creation and His command. For this reason, (Al-Hakim, the Wise) is among His Most Beautiful Names. Wisdom is among His exalted attributes, and the Sharia that proceeds from His command is founded upon wisdom. The Messenger who was sent with it was sent with the Book and the wisdom. Wisdom is the Sunnah of the Messenger, and it includes knowledge of the truth, acting upon it, informing about it, and commanding it. All of this is called wisdom. It is related in a report: "Wisdom is the lost property of the believer." And in a hadith: "Indeed, some poetry is wisdom." Just as nothing that is decreed escapes His knowledge, power and will, so likewise nothing escapes His wisdom and praiseworthiness. He is praised for everything in the universe, good and evil, with a praise that He deserves by His very essence, and from Him proceed His creation and His command. The source of all of that is wisdom, so denying wisdom is in reality a denial of His praise. And Allah knows best. End of quotation.

And Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, said, in the course of some of his fatawa, concerning the reality of arguing with the decree and destiny, the following text:

Indeed, these Qadariyya-Jabriyya-Jahmiyya (those who deny human agency and hold that man is compelled, and the Jahmiyya who denied divine attributes), the people who become absorbed in (the oneness of Lordship), the reality of their statement is of the same kind as the statement of the polytheists who said: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything﴾ [Al-An'am: 148], and so on. When these polytheists rejected what the messengers were sent with of commands and prohibitions, and they rejected monotheism, which is the worship of Allah alone with no partner, while they acknowledged the oneness of Lordship and that Allah is the Creator of everything, there remained among them no distinction, from the standpoint of Allah, the Exalted, between what is commanded and what is forbidden. So they said: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything﴾. This is true, for if Allah had willed that this not occur, it would not have occurred. But what benefit is this to them? Its ultimate result is that this polytheism and prohibition are by decree, and it does not follow that, if something is decreed, it is beloved and pleasing to Allah. They have no knowledge that Allah commanded it, nor that He loves it, nor that He is pleased with it. Rather, they are only upon conjecture and guesswork. End of quotation.

And some of the verifying scholars said concerning the reality of belief:

It is established by proof that the power of Allah, Exalted is He, operates upon possible things by will and choice. The will does not depart from what is revealed by knowledge of the places of wisdom and the aspects of order. He is the Creator of everything, and to Him the whole matter returns. Among the possible things that wisdom and order required is the existence of a created being who has power, will and knowledge, who acts by his power whatever his will moves him toward, according to his knowledge of the aspects of benefit and advantage for himself. This being is man. According to some, this is the meaning of his being the vicegerent of Allah on earth, who cultivates it, manifests the wisdom of Allah and the wondrous secrets within it, and establishes His wise laws, until His perfection is known through knowledge of the perfection of His craftsmanship. Man continues to manifest the signs of these creatures moment after moment, and no one knows the extent of that except Allah, Exalted is He. It is well known that the vicegerency is specific to certain individuals of mankind, namely the prophets, peace be upon them. Neither of the two views requires that Allah, Exalted is He, appointed them as vicegerents because He had need of that. Far is He above that.

Al-Baydawi said, in "a statement that every prophet is a vicegerent": He appointed them to cultivate the earth, to govern people, to perfect their souls, and to carry out His command among them, not because He, Exalted is He, has need of someone to act in His place, but because of the deficiency of those upon whom the vicegerency is conferred in receiving His overflow and in receiving His command without an intermediary. For this reason, He did not make an angel a prophet, as He said: ﴿Had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾. End of quotation. And likewise, if we say that the whole species is vicegerent in the earthly worlds.

From each of the two views it is known that in man there is a meaning that is not found in others. If the creation of an angel does not assist in guiding people, because he is not of their kind and it is not possible for each individual to receive from him, then likewise his creation does not assist. Nor is it part of its function to manifest the properties and powers of bodies and the aspects of benefiting from them. And if the bringing into existence of a creature, in the manner we have described in the creation of man, were not possible, it would not have come into existence. No one denies its being as we have described except one who denies sense perception and intuition, and these two are the basis of every proof. Such a person is not addressed, nor is he asked to affirm anything at all.

Thus, we have two matters whose certainty is definite:

The first: that man acts by a power and a will that his knowledge moves to act or to refrain and withhold. This is self-evident.

The second: that Allah is the Creator in whose hand is the dominion of everything. This is theoretical. From these two definite matters arise two theoretical questions:

The first: What is the difference between the knowledge, will and power of Allah, Exalted is He, and the knowledge, will and power of man? The answer has several aspects:

The first: the attributes of Allah are eternal by His eternity, so they are established for Him by His essence. The attributes of man are created with his creation, and they are bestowed upon him by Allah, Exalted is He, as his essence is.

The second: the knowledge of Allah encompasses everything. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. As for man, he has been given only a little knowledge. The will of Allah, Exalted is He, does not change and does not accept cancellation, because it is from complete knowledge. Unlike the will of man, which wavers because of his hesitation about knowing a thing, is cancelled when the error in the knowledge upon which it was built becomes apparent, and is renewed when new knowledge comes to one who did not have it before. The power of Allah, Exalted is He, operates upon every possible thing, so He does everything He knows to contain wisdom. The power of man has no operation or acquisition except in the least of the possible things. How many matters there are whose benefit and advantage for him he knows, yet he cannot undertake them.

The third: the attributes of man are subject to weakness and to cessation, while the attributes of Allah, Exalted is He, are everlasting, just as they are without beginning. In sum, the sharing between the attributes of Allah, Exalted is He, and the attributes of His servants is only in the name, not in the reality, as some have claimed. Thus refuted is the claim of one who said that affirming that the acts proceeding from man are by his power and will requires that he be a partner with Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe﴾ [As-Saffat: 180].

The second question, which is the knot of the contract and the touchstone of the critic: that decree (qada') is an expression for the connection of the knowledge or will of Allah, Exalted is He, in eternity, that a thing will occur in a specific manner among the possible manners, and that destiny (qadar) is the occurrence of things in accordance with what was preceded in eternity.

Among the things to which decree and destiny are connected are the voluntary acts of servants. So if a binding decree has preceded, that Zayd will live as a disbeliever and die as a disbeliever, what is the meaning of demanding of him belief when it is beyond his capacity? And in reality and in fact it cannot proceed from him, because in truth he is compelled to disbelief in the form of one who chooses it? As some have said.

The answer to this is: that the connection of knowledge and will to the fact that so-and-so does such-and-such does not contradict his doing it by choice, unless the knowledge were connected to his doing it under compulsion, like the movement of one who trembles, for example. But the voluntary acts of servants have been preceded in the decree by the fact that they occur voluntarily, that is, by the will of their doers, not against their will. And by this, the legal obligation is valid, and legislation is not in vain or idle.

There is another aspect of the answer: if the foreknowledge or will that a doer does such-and-such necessitated that this doer be compelled to his act, then the Necessary Existent, Exalted and Sanctified is He, would be compelled in all His acts, because the eternal knowledge has been connected to that, and whatever sound knowledge is connected to must occur.

Thus it becomes clear from this that the Jabriyya and those who followed them have neglected the meaning of choice, their views have been confused, so they denied sense perception and intuition, they opposed evidence and proof, they nullified the laws and religions, and they imagined that they exalt Allah, but they did not measure Him by His true measure, nor did they understand the secret of His prohibition and His command. They emboldened the ignorant to disclaim responsibility for sins and burdens, to claim innocence for themselves, and to put the blame on the decree and destiny. That is an absolving of themselves from Allah, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah. Rather, that is an incitement for man to plunge into wickedness and disobedience. How strange it is that they made the greatest deterrent into an incitement, which is the belief in the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah concerning things! Is it not the nature of one whose innate disposition has not been corrupted by compulsion, and whose insight has not been darkened by ignorance, that his greatest refiner of his soul and educator of his intellect and sense is his belief that Allah knows what is secret and what is public, what is manifest and what is hidden, and that He sees him and watches over him? Indeed! Excellence is that you worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you. As for those who have strayed from the path and followed corrupt interpretation, they say as those before them said, and Allah has related that to us in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Those who associated will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated"﴾ [Al-An'am: 148], and so on. Observe how the All-Knowing, All-Wise charged them with ignorance, and made their argument from destiny one of the causes of the coming of calamity and affliction upon them.

In this measure there is sufficiency for one whose light of innate disposition has not been extinguished before him. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[150] ﴿Say: "Bring forward your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this." Then if they testify, do not testify along with them, and do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs and of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who set up equals to their Lord.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Bring forward your witnesses"﴾, meaning: bring them here. ﴿"who testify that Allah has forbidden this"﴾, meaning what you say of the cattle and the tilth. By "their witnesses" is meant their leaders who support their claim. They were commanded to bring them forward so that the proof would be binding on them, and so that, when they fall silent, their misguidance would become evident, and that they have no basis to hold onto, as with one who follows them blindly, so that the truth is confirmed and falsehood is nullified. ﴿"Then if they testify"﴾, meaning after they have been brought forward, that Allah has forbidden this: ﴿"then do not testify along with them"﴾, meaning do not accept what they testify to, and do not confirm them, because you know of their fabrication against Allah and their walking after their own desires.

In al-Qasimi's citation of *al-'Inayah*: "fa-la tashhad" (do not testify) is an *isti'arah tab'iyyah* (a dependent metaphor, in which the metaphor is embedded in a verb or derived form). It has been said that it is a *majaz mursal* (a metonymy using a more general or related term), mentioning the necessary consequence and intending what it necessitates, since testifying is a necessary consequence of acceptance. It has also been said that it is a *kinayah* (an allusion or indirect expression). And it has been said that it is a *mushakalah* (a figure in which a word is used because of its association with another word in the same context).

﴿"and do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs and of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who set up equals to their Lord"﴾ This is the placing of an apparent noun in the place of a pronoun, to indicate that whoever denies the signs of Allah and sets up others as equal to Him, meaning he makes idols equal to Him, is then merely following his desire, because if he were following evidence he would be none other than one who affirms the signs and professes the oneness of Allah, exalted is He.

When Allah, exalted is He, had made clear the corruption of what they claimed, namely that their polytheism, the polytheism of their fathers, and their prohibition of what they forbade were by the command and will of Allah, by the manifest inability of them to produce anything they could hold to in this matter, and to bring forward witnesses who would testify to it, after they had been challenged to do so repeatedly, He commanded the Messenger to make clear to them the prohibited things that the situation required him to explain.

**[151]** ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him; be good to your parents; do not kill your children because of poverty — We provide for you and for them; do not approach indecencies, whether open or hidden; and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. This He has enjoined upon you, so that you may understand."﴾

Almighty God said: ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him"﴾, meaning idols. ﴿And be good to your parents﴾, i.e., treat your parents with goodness. Al-Hakim (al-Ḥākim) said: "Goodness (iḥsān) is that which goes beyond the limit of disobedience (ʿuqūq)." A similar example is His saying: ﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ [Luqman: 15]. Since making goodness obligatory amounts to forbidding the abandonment of goodness, it is mentioned among the prohibitions. The same applies to the commands that follow it, for a command to do something necessarily entails a prohibition of its opposite; indeed, according to some, it is identical with it. It is as if the commands were mentioned while their necessary implications were intended. One of the secrets of this, here—I mean placing "and be good to your parents" in the position of "prohibition of harming them"—is emphasis and an indication that refraining from harming them is not sufficient in fulfilling their rights, unlike the case of others.

﴿And do not kill your children because of poverty﴾, i.e., on account of poverty, or out of fear of it. The meaning of "killing" here is burying daughters alive, which the Arabs used to do in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). So God forbade them from that and prohibited it for them. ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾, because the sustenance of servants is the responsibility of their master.

﴿And do not approach indecencies﴾, meaning fornication (zina), based on His saying: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an indecency﴾ [al-Isra': 32]. The plural form was used either intending to forbid its various kinds, or for emphasis in view of the multiplicity of those who commit it. ﴿Whether open or hidden﴾, meaning its public and its secret forms. ﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden﴾, i.e., killing it on account of its faith or its safe-conduct (amān). ﴿Except by right﴾, i.e., by justice, meaning by retaliation (qawd), stoning, and apostasy (ridda). ﴿This He has enjoined upon you﴾, out of gentleness and compassion. ﴿So that you may understand﴾, meaning: so that you may understand its enormity before God Almighty, and thus refrain from committing it.

Al-Mahayimi (al-Mahāyimī) said: Associating partners with God, disobedience to parents, and killing children for fear of poverty all arise from ignorance of what is involved in associating partners—belittling the Benefactor who brought things into existence—and of what is involved in harming one's parents—repaying goodness with harm—and of approaching indecencies, which stems from following desire, and of killing, which stems from following anger. All of these are opposites of intellect ('aql).

[p. 2566] **Note:**

Some of the Zaydiyyah (al-Zaydiyya) said: God's saying ﴿out of poverty﴾ came out according to the customary situation; otherwise, it is forbidden whether one fears poverty or not, and the verse indicates the prohibition of killing children in general.

Al-Hakim said: Thus, taking medicine to kill a fetus is included in this. Imam Yahya said: If the soul has been breathed into it, [it is forbidden]; but if it is without destroying the sperm-drop, the clot, or the lump of flesh before the soul is breathed into it, [it is permissible]. In al-Ahkam (the book of rulings), it is obligatory for a woman whose menstruation has ceased to avoid medicines that endanger the fetus, if she is a married woman. And in His saying ﴿This He has enjoined upon you﴾ there is an emphasis on the obligation of what was mentioned before. End of quote.

**Subtle point:**

Al-Qashani (al-Qāshānī) said: Since the discourse was with the polytheists concerning the prohibition of good things, He enumerated the prohibited matters so that the permitted ones might be inferred from them. He thus restricted all kinds of virtues to the prohibition of the genera of vices, and began with the prohibition of the vice of the rational (intellectual) faculty, which is the most noble of them. Its vice is the greatest of the major sins, entailing all vices, unlike the vice of its two siblings, the bestial and the predatory faculties. So He said: ﴿that you associate nothing with Him﴾, for associating partners is one of the errors of this faculty in its perception, and its failure to use reason and grasp proof. He followed it with goodness to parents, for knowledge of their rights comes after knowledge of God in creation and lordship, since they are the two near causes in existence and upbringing, and the two intermediaries God made manifestations of His attributes of creation and lordship. Hence it was said: "Whoever obeys his parents has obeyed God and His Messenger." Thus disobedience to them comes right after association, and ignorance of their rights arises only from ignorance of God's rights and of knowledge of His attributes. Then came the prohibition of killing children out of fear of poverty, for committing that arises only from ignorance and blindness regarding God's causation of sustenance for every creature, and that the provisions of servants are in His hand: He extends sustenance to whomever He wills and restricts it. It also arises from being veiled from the secret of divine decree, so that one does not know that provisions are determined in proportion to lifespans, like the appointed terms. The first of these vices arises only from error in knowing God's essence; the second from error in knowing His attributes; the third from error in knowing His acts. Thus one commits these three vices only if he is inverted and veiled from God's essence, attributes, and acts; and these veils are the mother and foundation of vices. Then He clarified the vice of the bestial faculty, since its vice is more evident and older, saying: ﴿and do not approach indecencies﴾. Then He alluded to the vice of the predatory faculty with His saying: ﴿and do not kill the soul﴾, and so on.

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[152] ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best, until he reaches his maturity. And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a relative. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. This He has instructed you, that you may remember.﴾

As for His exalted saying: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan﴾, meaning: in any manner whatsoever. ﴿Except in the way that is best﴾, meaning: by the means that is best, that is, that is most beneficial to him, such as investing it, preserving it, or taking it as a loan. Not by consuming it, spending it on your own purposes, or wasting it, for that is most vile. We have already mentioned an outline of what is permitted to the guardian of an orphan or his executor in His exalted saying in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:6]. Abu Dawud related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "When Allah revealed: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan﴾ [the verse], and: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:10] [the verse], those who had orphans in their charge set aside their food from his food and his drink from his drink. Then some of his food would be left over and kept for him until he ate it or it spoiled. This was hard for them, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah revealed: ﴿And they ask you about orphans. Say: Reforming them is best. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:220], so they mixed their food with his food and their drink with his drink."

It has been said: Allah specified the property of the orphan for mention only because he cannot defend himself or his property, neither he nor anyone else. Thus the desires for his property are stronger. Therefore the prohibition concerning it is emphasized, since it is the protection and the preliminary step to it, and He commanded its growth ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾, meaning: his strength by which he is able to preserve it and manage it. This is a limit to what is understood from the exception, not to the prohibition, as if it were said: Guard it until he becomes a mature and sound-minded adult. Then, at that point, hand it over to him, as in His exalted saying: ﴿But if you perceive in them sound judgment, then deliver to them their property﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:6]. "Ashudd" is the plural of "shiddah," like ni'mah and an'um, or of "shadd," like kalb and aklub, or of "shidd," like sirr and asur. It has also been said that it is a singular noun, like ankuk.

﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾, meaning: with justice and equality in taking and giving. Allah has threatened those who abandon this in His exalted saying: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss. Do they not think that they will be resurrected, on a tremendous Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 83:1–6].

Ibn Kathir said: Allah has destroyed a nation of the nations that used to cheat in measure. At-Tirmidhi related from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people of measure and weight: "Indeed you have been entrusted with two matters in which the earlier nations before you were destroyed." Then he declared it weak, but authenticated it as a statement of Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh related something similar with a raised chain, and its wording is: "Indeed you, O company of clients, Allah has given you glad tidings of two qualities, by which the previous generations were destroyed: by the measure and the weight."

﴿We do not burden any soul﴾, meaning: at the time of measuring and weighing, ﴿except according to its capacity﴾, meaning: its effort in justice. This interjection came immediately after the command to justice, to show that observing the limit of justice, which has no excess and no deficiency, is among the things that involve hardship because of the difficulty of observing it. So He commanded striving to the extent of capacity, and that which lies beyond it is pardoned. Ibn Mardawayh related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever, at his hand, gives full measure and weight with justice, [and] Allah knows the soundness of his intention in fulfilling them both, he will not be called to account."

Ibn al-Musayyab said: That is the interpretation of "according to its capacity."

Ibn Kathir said: This is a mursal and strange report.

In al-'Inayah: It is possible that His exalted saying ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾ refers to what came before, meaning: everything We have obligated you with is possible, and We do not burden with what cannot be borne. End of quote. The first is more preferable.

﴿And when you speak﴾, meaning: in a judgment, testimony, or the like, ﴿be just﴾, meaning: in them, that is, say nothing but the truth. ﴿Even if﴾, meaning: the one spoken to or about, ﴿it concerns a relative﴾, meaning: one of your kin. So do not lean in speech toward him or against him, either by addition or by subtraction.

Some of the Zaydiyyah said: The meaning of His exalted saying ﴿And when you speak, be just﴾ is: be truthful in your speech. He said: This expression is among the wondrous things in the sweetness of its wording and the fewness of its letters, and in its gathering of many matters: acknowledgment, testimony, bequests, enjoining good and forbidding evil, fatwas, rulings, and doctrines.

Then He emphasized this, and made clear that justice in speech is obligatory even if the one addressed is a relative, as in His exalted saying: ﴿Even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:135].

﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah﴾, meaning: what has been enjoined upon you of the matters enumerated, or any covenant whatsoever, so that what was mentioned enters into it first and foremost. Or it means what you have pledged to Allah through oaths and vows. ﴿This﴾ refers to what has been mentioned in these verses. ﴿He has instructed you with it﴾, meaning: He has commanded you to act upon it in the Book. ﴿That you may remember﴾, meaning: that you may take heed. In His exalted saying ﴿This He has instructed you with it﴾ there is another emphasis.

**The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[153] ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it; and do not follow the (other) ways, lest they scatter you from His way. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may be righteous.﴾

﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it﴾ is recited with the hamza of (anna) pronounced open and the nun doubled. Its grammatical position, together with what follows it, is in the genitive by deletion of the particle of causation (lam al-'illa, "the particle expressing reason"). The meaning is: "And because this which I have enjoined upon you, of commands and prohibitions, is My path and My religion, which I have approved for My servants as upright, with no crookedness in it, so act upon it." It is also permitted that its grammatical position, together with what follows it, be in the accusative, governed by (what He has forbidden), meaning: "And I recite to you that this is My path." It is also recited with the hamza kasra, as a resumption (istinaf) of speech.

﴿and do not follow the (other) ways﴾ means the differing religions, or the paths of innovation (bid'ah) and misguidance.

﴿lest they scatter you from His way﴾ means: lest they separate you from His straight path, which is the religion of Islam that He has approved for His servants.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew a line for us and then said: 'This is the path of Allah.' Then he drew lines to its right and to its left and said: 'These are paths, over each one of which is a devil calling to it.' Then he recited: ﴿And that this is My path, straight...﴾, the verse..." It was also narrated by al-Hakim, who authenticated it.

**Subtleties:**

Ilkiya al-Harrasi said: The verse is evidence for the prohibition of speculation and opinion where there is an explicit text.

Ibn Kathir said: He said "His way" in the singular because the truth is one; and for this reason He used the plural "the ways", because they are scattered and branching. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out from the darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the taghut; they bring them out from the light into the darknesses﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257].

Ibn 'Atiyya said: These ways encompass Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and all the other religious communities, as well as the people of innovation and misguidance, including the people of desires and of deviation in the branches of law, and others among the people of excessive depth in disputation and of plunging into theological discourse. All of these are exposed to error and are a source of corrupt belief.

Qatada said: Know that the path is one single path: the community of guidance, and its destination is Paradise. And Iblis invented scattered paths: the community of misguidance, and their destination is the Fire.

Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse and concerning His saying: ﴿that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [ash-Shura: 13], that he said: "Inform them that those before them were destroyed only through disputation and quarrels over the religion of Allah."

﴿That﴾ refers to what has been mentioned of following His path, the Exalted, and abandoning the following of all the other ways: ﴿is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may be righteous﴾, meaning: that you may avoid following disbelief and misguidance. This also contains emphasis.

al-Tirmidhi narrated and graded it good, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Whoever wishes to look at the testament of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), upon which is his seal, let him recite these verses: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you not associate anything with Him﴾ [al-An'am: 151] — to His saying — ﴿that you may be righteous﴾."

al-Hakim narrated and authenticated, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "In al-An'am there are clear verses, which are the Mother of the Book," then he recited: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ [al-An'am: 151], the verses.

al-Hakim narrated and authenticated, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Which of you will pledge allegiance to me upon these three verses?" Then he recited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ [al-An'am: 151], until he finished the three verses. Then he said: "Whoever fulfils them, his reward is upon Allah. Whoever falls short in any of them, and Allah seizes him for it in this world, that will be his punishment. And whoever has it deferred to the Hereafter, his matter is with Allah: if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will pardon him."

**Subtlety:**

al-Nasafi said: He first mentioned (you may understand, ta'qilun), then (you may remember, tadhakkarun), then (you may be righteous, tattaqun), because when they understand, they reflect, then they remember, that is, they take admonition, and so they guard against the prohibited things. End of quotation.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[154] ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete [in blessing] upon the one who did good, and as an explanation of all things, and as guidance and mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.﴾

﴿Then We gave﴾ i.e., We bestowed: ﴿Moses the Book﴾, meaning the Torah: ﴿complete upon the one who did good﴾. It is read with a fatha on the nun, as a past-tense verb whose subject is either a pronoun referring to (alladhi, "the one who"), meaning: complete as honour and blessing upon the one who did good, i.e., upon whoever was a doer of good and righteous, intending the category of the good-doers. This is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud): (upon those who did good). Or the subject is a pronoun referring to Moses, peace be upon him, and its object is omitted, meaning: a completion of honour upon the servant who did good in conveying and in everything he was commanded to do. Or: complete upon the one who (Moses) did good in knowledge and laws, from (aḥsana al-shayʾ), when one mastered knowledge of it, i.e., an increase upon his knowledge in the manner of perfecting. On the first reading, (tamāman) is in the position of an object of purpose (al-mafʿūl lahu). The omission of the lam is permitted because it carries the meaning of (itmāman, "completing"), or it is a verbal noun for the verb (ātaynā) from its meaning, since giving the Book is a completion of the blessing. It is as if it were said: We completed the blessing with a completion. So (tamām) is in the sense of (itmām), like (nabāt) in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And God made you grow from the earth as a growth﴾ [Nuh: 17]; or its origin is (ītāʾ tamām, "giving of completion"). On the second reading, it is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of the Book. Yahya ibn Yaʿmar read (upon the one who is ʾaḥsanu) with a raised ending, meaning: upon the one which is best, or upon the manner in which the Book is best. Then (tamāman) is a state of the Book in the sense of (tāmman), meaning: the Book being complete, existing in the best possible form. Ibn Jarir said: "This is a reading I do not consider permissible to recite, although it has a valid grammatical basis in Arabic." ﴿And an explanation of all things﴾: i.e., and a detailed clarification of everything the Children of Israel need in religion: ﴿and guidance﴾ for them to their Lord in following His path: ﴿and mercy﴾ upon them by pouring out benefits: ﴿that they﴾, i.e., the People of the Book: ﴿might believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾, i.e., affirm His meeting for recompense.

A subtle point:

Al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil": He used His saying, ﴿Then We gave﴾, as evidence for those who say that (thumma, "then") does not indicate sequence. End.

Ibn Kathir said: "Thumma here serves to connect one report after another, not for sequence, as the poet said:

"Say to the one who was chief, then his father became chief, then his grandfather before that became chief."

Abu al-Suʿud said: "Thumma is for delay in reports, as in your saying: 'I was told what you did today, then what you did yesterday is more amazing.' Or it indicates a difference in rank, as if it were said: That is what He enjoined upon you long ago and recently. Then greater than that is that We gave Moses the Torah, for giving it includes the aforementioned charge and other things, and is greater than merely enjoining it alone." End.

Then he pointed out that the Torah, although it was complete upon the best path, the Qur'an is more complete than it and more excellent in goodness. So it is more deserving of being followed, and he said:

(p-2574) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[155] ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and fear God that you may be shown mercy﴾

﴿And this﴾, i.e., the Qur'an: ﴿is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾, more beneficial than the Torah in religion and in worldly affairs. ﴿So follow it﴾, i.e., act upon what is in it of commands, prohibitions and rulings. ﴿And fear God﴾, meaning: avoid opposing it and following other than it, since it abrogates what came before it. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾, i.e., so that you may be granted mercy through following it, which is acting upon what is in it. In this there is an indication that there is no mercy in following what has been abrogated, even if its adherent believes in the meeting with his Lord.

Some of the Zaydiyyah (the Zaydi school) said: In His, the Exalted's, saying ﴿so follow it﴾ there is evidence for the obligation of learning the Qur'an so that following it becomes possible. However, it is like the other sciences: it is a collective obligation (fard kifaya), except for what is incumbent upon every accountable person individually, such as learning what the prayer cannot be valid without, for that is obligatory upon him. End of quotation.

A subtle point:

Ibn Kathir said: He often pairs the two Books, as in His saying: ﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy, and this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 12], and His saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book which Moses brought﴾ [al-An'am: 91], then He said: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾, to the end of the verse. (p-2575) And His, the Exalted's, saying reporting about the polytheists: ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said: Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?﴾ [al-Qasas: 48], and His saying reporting about the jinn that they said: ﴿O our people, we have heard a Book sent down after Moses, confirming what is before it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], to the end of the verse.

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[156] ﴿Lest you should say: "The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of their study."﴾

﴿Lest you should say﴾ is a reason for (We sent it down). That is: out of aversion that you should say on the Day of Resurrection, or so that you would not say: ﴿"The Book was only sent down to two groups before us"﴾, namely the Jews and the Christians, ﴿"and we were indeed unaware of their study"﴾, of the recitation of their Book, ﴿unaware﴾, having no knowledge of anything of it, because it was not in our language.

Abu al-Su'ud said: Their purpose by this is to repel what would be raised against them, that its being sent down to the two groups does not contradict the generality of its rulings. So why did you not act upon its general rulings? The meaning is: "We did not know what was in their Book, since it was not in our language, so that we could receive from it those general rulings and preserve them, even though it was not revealed to us." Thereby it becomes clear that their excuse, although they were not commanded to follow what is in the two Books, since they include the mentioned rulings that encompass all nations, is cut off by the sending down of the Qur'an, since it also includes them, not merely the rest of the laws and rulings. End.

(p-٢٥٧٦) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[157] ﴿Or [lest] you should say: "If the Book had only been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than they." Now there has come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy. So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our signs with a terrible punishment, for what they used to turn away.﴾

﴿Or [lest] you should say: "If the Book had only been revealed to us﴾, i.e., as it was revealed to them. ﴿we would have been better guided than they﴾, i.e., to the truth, and quicker than they to respond to the Messenger, because of our greater intelligence and our diligence in acting. ﴿Now there has come to you﴾. Abu al-Su'ud said: It is connected to a omitted element indicated by the eloquent fa' (al-fa' al-fasihah, the fa' that signals an implied condition or clause). It is either a cause for that, i.e., "Do not make excuses with this, for there has come to you," or it is a condition for it, i.e., "If you are truthful about what you used to promise yourselves, namely that you would be better guided than the two groups, on the assumption that the Book had been revealed to you, then what you supposed has happened, and there has come to you" ﴿clear evidence﴾, i.e., a clear book of proof ﴿from your Lord﴾. It is connected to (there has come to you), or to an omitted element serving as a qualifier of (clear evidence), i.e., clear evidence issuing from Him, exalted is He, in which no magic can be suspected. ﴿and guidance﴾, by establishing proofs and removing doubts. ﴿and mercy﴾, by bestowing benefits and facilitating your path and making it easy for you to reach the most noble perfections. ﴿So who is more unjust﴾. Abu al-Su'ud said: The fa' is for the ordering of what follows upon what precedes, for the coming of the Qur'an, which contains guidance and mercy, necessitates the utmost injustice of those who deny it. I.e., and since the matter is so: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them﴾, i.e., who diverts people and prevents them from them. Thus he combines error with leading others astray. The meaning is a denial that anyone could be more unjust than him or equal to him. ﴿We will recompense those who turn away﴾ from people ﴿from Our signs﴾, i.e., which, had they not turned away from them, they would have recognized their inimitability. ﴿with a terrible punishment﴾, i.e., the evil punishment. ﴿for what they used to turn away.﴾ This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah, We shall increase them in punishment upon punishment for what they used to spread corruption﴾ [al-Nahl: 88].

(p-2577) The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:
[158] ﴿Are they waiting for anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come? On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith. Say: "Wait, indeed we are waiting."﴾

﴿Are they waiting﴾ meaning: We have established the proofs of Divine Oneness and the confirmation of prophethood, and We have nullified the misguidance they held to. So what are these people waiting for, after their denial of the Messengers, their rejection of the Qur'an, and their turning away from the signs of God?

Al-Baydawi said: meaning the people of Mecca, who were not in fact waiting for this, but since it would befall them as it befalls one who is waiting, they were likened to those who wait. ﴿unless the angels come to them, or your Lord comes﴾ meaning, for judgment and the decisive settling of matters among creation on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Kathir said: That occurs on the Day of Resurrection. The discussion of the meaning of this verse has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah at His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Are they waiting for anything but that God should come to them in canopies of cloud?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210], with what is sufficient there.

The position of the early generation (al-salaf) is to pass these matters on without asking how (imrar dhalika bila kayf), as has passed repeatedly.

It was said: "unless the angels come to them," i.e., the angels of death to seize their souls. ﴿Or some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, and that is before the Day of Resurrection, being among the portents and signs of the Hour, when they see something of that. As al-Bukhari narrated in his tafsir of this verse, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its west. When people see it, all those on the earth will believe (p-2578) — that is the time when faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before." Muslim also narrated it. And in Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three things, when they come forth, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjal, and the beast of the earth."

﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before﴾: the phrase "a soul" (nafsan) is a qualifier. ﴿or had not earned good through its faith﴾ is conjoined to "had believed" (amanat). The meaning is that when some of the portents of the Hour come — and it is a compelling, forcing sign — the time of obligation has passed with it, so faith then does not benefit a soul that had not previously put forward its faith before the signs appeared, or one that had put forward faith but had not earned good through it because of its wickedness. So its repentance then is of no avail.

Al-Tabari said: The meaning of the verse is: faith after the rising will not benefit an unbeliever who had not believed before the rising, and good deeds after the rising will not benefit a believer who had not done righteous deeds before the rising; because the ruling on faith and righteous deeds at that time is the ruling on one who believes or acts at the moment of the death-rattle (al-gharghara), and that avails nothing, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir: 85], and as is established in the authentic hadith: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of a servant so long as he has not reached the death-rattle." End of quote.

In summary: the meaning is that faith does not benefit one who was a polytheist, and the repentance of a wicked person is not accepted when this mighty sign appears, which compels them to faith and repentance, because the time of obligation has gone.

(p-2579) Al-Dahhak said: Whoever is overtaken by some of the signs while he is doing righteous deeds together with his faith, Allah accepts from him the righteous deed after the revelation of the verse, just as He accepted it before that. As for one who believes after polytheism or repents from disobedience at the appearance of this verse, it is not accepted from him, because it is a state of compulsion. Just as if Allah sent a punishment upon a nation and they believed and affirmed, their faith would not benefit them, because they witnessed the terrors and hardships that compel them to faith and repentance.

Ibn Kathir said: If an unbeliever initiates faith on that day, it is not accepted from him.
