As for one who was already a believer, it is accepted; if he was a reformer in his deeds, he has a great good; and if he was not a reformer, and then makes a repentance at that time, his repentance is not accepted from him, as the hadiths indicate. And upon this is understood His statement, exalted is He: ﴿or had earned good through its faith﴾, meaning: earning of righteous deeds is not accepted from it if he had not been practicing them before. End of quote.

The hadiths referred to include what Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever repents before the sun rises from its west, Allah will accept his repentance." Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it (p-2580) from Safwan ibn Assal al-Muradi, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is a gate on the side of the west, the breadth of which is a journey — or he said: a rider travels across its breadth — forty or seventy years. Allah created it on the day He created the heavens and the earth, open for repentance; it is not closed until the sun rises from it." And Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i have, from the hadith of Mu'awiyah, traced to the Prophet: "Repentance will continue to be accepted until the sun rises from its west."

Ibn Hajar said: its isnad is good. Ahmad, al-Darimi and Abd ibn Humayd also narrated it from the same hadith (p-2581) with the wording: "Repentance does not cease until the sun rises from its west." Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn al-Sa'di that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Emigration does not cease as long as the enemy is being fought." Then Mu'awiyah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Emigration is of two kinds: one of them is that you forsake evil deeds, and the other is that you emigrate to Allah and His Messenger. It does not cease so long as repentance is accepted; repentance remains accepted until the sun rises from the west. When it rises, every heart is sealed with what is in it, and people are relieved of works."

Ibn Kathir said: This hadith has a good isnad, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it.

Here are some issues:

First: The majority held that what is meant by "some" (al-ba'd) in the verse is the rising of the sun from its west, as in the hadith of the two Sahihs mentioned earlier. It is not said that the hadith of Muslim, "Three things, when they come forth, faith will not benefit a soul...", contradicts this. As to whether that applies to the emergence of the Dajjal, there is doubt, because the descent of 'Isa ﷺ comes after him, and in his time there is much good, worldly and otherworldly, so faith is accepted at that time. We say: there is no contradiction. For "some" in the verse, if it means a number of signs, then the rising of the sun is the last of them, the one by which non-acceptance is definitely realised; and if it means one of the signs, then it is to be understood as the specific one in the hadith, since it is the greatest of them. Thus in al-'Inayah.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: When the Prophet ﷺ reported in the authentic hadith that the impediment to acceptance is specified as the rising, it is not permissible to depart from it, and it is established that this is the meaning of the verse. End of quote.

Al-Qadi 'Iyad said: The meaning is: no repentance benefits after that; rather, each person's deeds are sealed in the state in which he is. The wisdom in that is that this is the first beginning of the onset of the Hour through the transformation of the upper world. So when that (p-2582) is witnessed, necessary faith arises by direct observation, and faith in the unseen is removed. It is then like faith at the death-rattle, which avails nothing. So the witnessing of the sun's rising from the west is similar to it.

Second: Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: The Mu'tazilah used this verse as evidence that faith does not benefit when no good is earned through it. This is rejected. There is an implied ellipsis in the speech. The meaning is: it does not benefit a soul that had not believed before its faith at that time, and does not benefit a soul that had not earned good before its repentance at that time.

Al-Shihab al-Samin said: People have answered that the meaning in the verse is that when some of the signs come, it does not benefit a disbelieving soul its faith which it produces at that time, nor a soul whose faith preceded but in which it earned no good. He has made the negation of faith conditional on one of two attributes: either the negation of prior faith alone, or prior faith together with the negation of earning good. The implication of a qualifying attribute is strong, so the verse is used as evidence for the position of the People of the Sunnah, and the Mu'tazilah's evidence is turned against them.

Ibn al-Munayyir answered in al-Intisaf, saying: This speech is among the forms of eloquence called (al-laff) "wrapping". Its underlying form is: On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul that had not been a believer before will benefit from its faith afterward, nor a soul that had not earned good before will benefit from the good it earns afterward. So he wrapped the two statements, making them one statement for brevity. By this formulation it becomes clear that it does not contradict the position of the People of Truth. After the signs appear, acquiring good does not benefit, even though earlier faith benefits in terms of eternal life. So the verse is more fitting as a refutation of the Mu'tazilah than as evidence for them.

Ibn al-Hajib said in his Amali: Faith before the coming of the verse is beneficial even if there is no other righteous deed. The meaning of the verse is: faith of a soul will not benefit it, nor its earning of righteous deeds, if it had not been a believer before the sign, or had not done deeds together with faith before it. It was abbreviated for knowledge.

Al-Tibi cited the statements of the imams on this. Then he said: The reliable view is what Ibn al-Munayyir and Ibn al-Hajib said. Its exposition: (p-2583) When Allah, exalted is He, addressed the obstinate with His statement: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it﴾ [al-An'am: 155], etc., He gave the reason for sending down by His statement: "lest you should say, 'The Book was only sent down...'" etc., to remove the excuse and establish the proof. And He followed it with His statement: "There has certainly come to you clear evidence..." etc., as a rebuke to them and a confirmation of what had preceded from those who sought to follow. Then He said: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies﴾ [al-An'am: 157], etc. That is: He sent down this luminous Book, revealing every doubt and guiding to the straight path and as a mercy from Allah to creation, so that they might make it provision for their return, in what they send ahead of faith and righteous deeds. But they made the thanks for the blessing to be denial of it and prevention of benefiting from it. Then He said: ﴿Are they waiting﴾, etc.; that is: these deniers are waiting for nothing but that the punishment of the world should come to them through the descent of the angels with the punishment that uproots their root, as happened to the nations before them; or the punishment of the Hereafter should come upon them through the appearance of some of its calamities. Then that earlier opportunity passes, and nothing benefits them of what had benefited them before, of faith, and likewise righteous deeds together with faith. So it is as if it were said: On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith nor from its earning of righteous deeds in its faith at that time, since it had not believed before, or had not earned good in its faith before. So in the verse there is wrapping (laff). But one of the two correspondents is dropped, with the help of the explanation (al-nashr). A parallel to this is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is proud, He will gather them all to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 172].

He said: This is what Ibn al-Munayyir meant by his words that this speech in eloquence is called (al-laff), and the meaning is: On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul that had not been a believer before that will benefit from its faith after that, (p-2584) nor will a soul benefit that had been a believer but had not done righteous deeds in its faith before that, from the righteous deeds it does after that. He said: By this formulation the position of the People of the Sunnah becomes clear. After the appearance of the sign, acquiring good does not benefit, namely because the door of repentance is closed and the scrolls and the recording angels are lifted; though what preceded the appearance of the sign of faith benefits its possessor in general.

Then al-Tibi said: "After this exposition, by the grace of God, I have found another verse that resembles this verse and fits this exposition in meaning and wording, without excess or deficiency. It is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [al-A'raf: 52] ﴿Do they await but its interpretation (ta'wil)? The day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: 'The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So are there any intercessors for us who will intercede for us, or could we be returned so that we might act differently from what we used to do?' They have certainly lost themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 53]. It becomes apparent from this that bare faith before the calamities of the Hour are unveiled is beneficial, and that faith accompanied by righteous deeds is more beneficial. As for after their occurrence, nothing benefits at all. And God knows best." End of the summary.

Third: In "al-Wajiz" (by al-Wahidi), regarding His saying, ﴿or your Lord comes﴾, it means: to decide the judgment among His creation. His coming is something we believe in without knowing its modality (kayf).

In the margins of "Jami' al-Bayan" (by al-Tabari): How could one not believe in His coming, exalted is He, on the Day of Resurrection, when the Qur'an has mentioned it in several places: ﴿Do they await but that God should come to them in canopies of cloud﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210]; ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [al-Fajr: 22]; ﴿Do they await but that the angels should come to them, or that the command of your Lord should come?﴾ [al-Nahl: 33]. What command could be more explicit than this in the Qur'an?

(p-2585) Al-Tabari narrated in his "Tafsir" from Ibn Abbas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, in the clouds there are openings through which God comes, enveloped." That is His saying: ﴿Do they await but that God should come to them in canopies of cloud, with the angels, and the matter be decided?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210].

Ikrimah said: "And the angels are around Him." So this is among the attributes of God, exalted is He. It is obligatory upon us to believe in its apparent meaning, and we affirm it as it has come, even if we do not know its modality. Our not knowing its modality is like our not knowing the modality of His essence. So we do not deny what we know because of our lack of knowledge of what we do not know. This is the doctrine of the early predecessors (salaf) of this community and the leading scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah. End of quotation.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Wait"﴾, meaning: say to these disbelievers, after clarifying the reality of the situation in a definitive manner: "Wait for what you are waiting for, namely the coming of one of the three matters, so that you may see what it is you are waiting for."

﴿Indeed, we too are waiting﴾, meaning: for that, so that we may witness what evil consequence will befall you.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the states of the People of the Book, following on from His explanation of the state of the polytheists with His words, glorified is He.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[159] ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, you (O Muhammad) are not in anything of them. Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion﴾ i.e., they differed concerning it, despite its unity in itself, so they made it scattered desires: ﴿and become sects﴾ i.e., factions, each faction following an imam for itself according to the dominance of those desires.

So they did not worship except through customs and innovations, and did not submit except to desires and deceptions. ﴿You are not in anything of them﴾ i.e., of their punishment. Or: you are free of them, protected in your esteem from their doctrines. Or the meaning is: leave them, for they have what they have.

Al-Qashani said: i.e., you are not in any part of guiding them to monotheism, since they are people of division, whose aspirations do not gather and whose intentions do not unite. ﴿Their affair is only with Allah﴾ i.e., regarding the recompense for their division and its repayment, not with you. ﴿Then He will inform them﴾ meaning, when they arrive on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿about what they used to do﴾ i.e., of evil deeds and division, through following desires. And He will recompense them for that with what matches their actions.

Note:

Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: this verse was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the verse that the Jews and the Christians differed before the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) and so they split up. Some of them applied the verse to the people of innovations, the people of doubts and the people of misguidance from this Ummah, and another applied it to the Kharijites, and they attributed to this a hadith which they traced back to the Prophet.

Ibn Kathir said: the chain of transmission for that is not sound. Then he said: The apparent meaning is that the verse is general for everyone who separated from the religion of Allah and opposed it, for Allah sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He might make it prevail over all religion, and his law is one, with no difference or division in it. So whoever differs regarding it (and they became sects) i.e., factions, like the adherents of religions, sects and desires and misguidances, then Allah, exalted is He, has absolved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of what they are in. This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you﴾ [al-Shura: 13], etc. And in a hadith: "We, the company of the prophets, are sons of one father (with different mothers); our religion is one." This is the Straight Path, and it is what the Messengers brought: the worship of Allah alone with no partner, and adherence to the law of the latest Messenger. Whatever contradicts that is misguidance, ignorance, opinions and desires, and the Messengers are free of them, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿you are not in anything of them﴾.

He then said: His words, exalted is He: ﴿Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do﴾ are like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated partners — Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Hajj: 17]. End of quote.

Abu Dawud narrated from Mu'awiyah who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us and said: 'Beware! The people before you from the People of the Book divided into seventy-two religious communities (millah). And this community will divide into seventy-three. Seventy-two will be in the Fire, and one in Paradise, and it is the Jama'ah (the main body).'" It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, and in it: "They said: Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Those who are upon what I am upon and my companions."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 160:

Then He explained His subtle kindness (lutf) in His judgment and justice on the Day of Resurrection. So He, exalted is He, said:

The discussion concerning the interpretation (ta'wil) of His statement, exalted is He:

[160] ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like of it, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like of it, and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾ meaning: comes on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds. ﴿Then he will have ten times the like of it﴾ meaning: ten good deeds of similar goodness.

Al-Mahayimi said: It is like one who presents a bunch of grapes to a sultan, who gives him in return according to what befits his sovereignty, without regard to the value of the bunch. End of quote.

Ten is the least of the multiples that He promised. Promises have also come of seventy, of seven hundred, and without measure. For this reason it has been said: the purpose of mentioning ten is to indicate abundance, not to limit the number to that specific figure. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾ meaning: with evil deeds: ﴿will not be recompensed except with the like of it﴾ in ugliness.

Al-Mahayimi said: Whoever disbelieves will be eternal in the Fire, for nothing is more hideous than his disbelief, like one who offends a sultan intending to kill him. And whoever commits a sin will be punished in proportion to it, like one who offends one of the common subjects. End of quote.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ meaning: by any reduction of reward or increase of punishment.

A subtle point (latifah):

Al-Qashani said, regarding His statement ﴿then he will have ten times the like of it﴾: This is the least degree of reward. That is because a good deed proceeds from the heart's manifestation, and an evil deed from the manifestation of the soul (nafs). So the least degree of its reward is that it reaches the station of the heart, which follows the station of the soul in ascent, just as tens follow units in numbers. As for the evil deed, there is no station lower than the station of the soul, so one inevitably descends to it, and he finds his recompense in the station of the soul in kind. From this it is known that reward is a matter of grace (fadl), for its recipient is increased by it, his readiness is illumined, and his receptivity to the outpouring of Truth increases. Thus he becomes stronger for multiples of what he did, and acquires multiplied rewards without end, through increased acceptance in performing each good deed and increased capacity and eagerness for good deeds as the outpouring increases, to a degree known only to God. As He said after mentioning multiples up to seven hundred: ﴿God multiplies for whom He wills﴾. And punishment is a matter of justice, since justice requires equality. Whoever does by means of the soul, if it is not pardoned, is requited by the soul in equal measure. End of quote.

(p-2589) Admonition (tanbih):

Many hadiths have come concerning the meaning of the verse. Imam Ahmad related from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, relating from his Lord, exalted is He: "Indeed your Lord, blessed and exalted is He, is Merciful. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him. If he does it, ten to seven hundred are recorded for him, up to many multiples. Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him. If he does it, one is recorded against him, or God erases it, and none perishes before God except one who is destroyed." Related by al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i. Imam Ahmad and Muslim related from Abu Dharr who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, blessed and exalted, says: Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have ten times its like, or more. Whoever comes with an evil deed, its recompense is its like, or I forgive. Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; whoever draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running; and whoever meets Me with earth's fill of sins, having not associated anything with Me, I meet him with its like in forgiveness." Al-Shaykhan related from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, exalted is He, says: When My servant intends to do an evil deed, do not record it against him until he does it; if he does it, record it with its like. And if he leaves it for My sake, record it for him as a good deed. And when he intends to do a good deed but does not do it, record it for him as a good deed; if he does it, record it for him as ten times its like up to seven hundred." This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Al-Tabarani related from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Friday is an expiation for what is between it and the next Friday, and three additional days. That is because God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have ten times its like﴾." Imam Ahmad related from Abu Dharr who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts three days of every month has fasted the whole of time." Related by al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi, who added: "So God revealed in His Book the confirmation of that: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have ten times its like﴾ — the day is for ten days." Other reports remain, but what has been mentioned is sufficient.

Then God, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform those who divided their religion (into sects) of what He, glorified is He, had bestowed upon him by guiding him to His upright religion, saying:

[p. 2591]

**On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[161] ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a religion of upright standing, the creed of Abraham, a ḥanīf; and he was not among the polytheists.﴾

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾, which is the religion of Islam that He has approved for His sincere servants. ﴿A religion﴾ (dīnan) is in the accusative as a substitute (badal) for the place of (ilā ṣirāṭin, "to a path"), because its meaning is: "He guided me to a path."

This is supported by His saying: "and guides them to Him on a straight path" (Q. 4:175). Alternatively, it is an object (mafʿūl) of an implied verb indicated by what is mentioned, i.e., "He made me know a religion." Or it is the object of (hadānī), and (hadā) takes two objects.

**Qiyaman** (upright) is an attribute (ṣifa) of (dīnan). It is read with a shadda (qayyiman), meaning: constant forever, which the sects and creeds do not alter, and which the laws and scriptures do not abrogate, establishing the affairs of this life and the Hereafter. It is also read without the shadda (qiyaman), as a verbal noun (maṣdar) described by it. Its origin is qiwam, like ʿiwaḍ, and it underwent i'lāl (vowel-change) in the same way as its verb, like al-qiyām.

**Millata Ibrāhīm** (the creed of Abraham), the one whose soundness is agreed upon, is that by which I turn away from everything other than Him, exalted is He. It is an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to (dīnan). **Ḥanīfan** (ḥanīf) is a state (ḥāl) of Ibrāhīm, meaning: inclining away from every religion and path that is false, in which there is any form of shirk.

His saying, exalted is He, **﴿and he was not among the polytheists﴾**, is a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ) affirming his purity, peace be upon him, from what those who divide their religion are upon, in belief and in action. That is: he was not of them in any matter of their religion, in its roots or its branches. This is stated explicitly in refutation of those who claim to be upon his creed: the polytheists of Makkah, the Jews, and the Christians. Abū al-Suʿūd conveyed this.

**Note:**

Ibn Kathīr said: This verse is like His saying: "Then We revealed to you: follow the creed of Abraham, a ḥanīf, and he was not among the polytheists" (Q. 16:123). That He was commanded to follow the ḥanīfiyya creed (the primordial monotheism) does not necessitate that Abraham was more perfect in it than he (the Prophet ﷺ), because he, peace be upon him, upheld it with great upholding, and it was perfected for him with complete perfection, such that no one before him reached this perfection. For this reason he said: "I am the seal of the Prophets, the master of the children of Adam without exception, and the bearer of the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd), which all creation desires, even the Friend (Abraham), peace be upon him."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abzā, from his father, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the morning, he would say: 'We have entered the morning upon the creed of Islam, the word of sincerity, the religion of our Prophet, and the creed of Abraham, a ḥanīf, and he was not among the polytheists.'"

Imam Aḥmad narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "It was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which of the religions is most beloved to Allah, exalted is He? He said: 'The ḥanīfiyya, the tolerant (samḥa).'"

Imam Aḥmad also narrated from ʿĀʾisha, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his chin upon my shoulders so that I could watch the Abyssinians' dance, until I was the one who grew weary, and I turned away from them." ʿĀʾisha said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me that day: 'Let the Jews know that in our religion there is latitude. Indeed, I have been sent with the tolerant ḥanīfiyya.'"

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 162:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[162] ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer﴾ because what is commanded here relates to the branches of the sacred laws (furu' al-shara'i'), while what preceded relates to their foundations (usul). That is: indeed my prayer is toward the Ka'bah. ﴿And my rites (nusuk)﴾ meaning my circumambulation (tawaf) and my slaughtering of offerings during the Hajj and the 'Umrah (ʿumrah, the lesser pilgrimage). Or, my worship in its entirety. ﴿And my living and my dying﴾ meaning what I do during my life and what I die upon of faith and righteous deeds; or the acts of obedience during life and the good deeds attributed to death, such as bequest (wasiyyah) and provision (tadbir). Or, living and dying themselves. ﴿Are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[163] ﴿He has no partner. And thus I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.﴾

﴿He has no partner﴾ means: sincerely for Allah, I do not associate anything else with Him in it. ﴿And thus﴾ means: by that statement or by sincerity. ﴿I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ means: the first of this community, because the submission (Islam) of every prophet precedes the submission of his community.

Ibn Kathir said: Exalted is He commands His Prophet to inform the polytheists who worship other than Allah, exalted is He, and slaughter for other than His name, that he opposes them in that. For his prayer is for Allah, and his sacrifice is in His name alone, with no partner.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[164] ﴿Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things? Every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ."﴾

﴿Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah"﴾, so that I would associate him in His worship. This is an answer to their call to him, peace be upon him, to worship their gods. In choosing the negation of seeking and desiring over the negation of worship there is an eloquence that is not hidden: ﴿while He is the Lord of all things﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) in a position of cause for the denial and evidence for it. That is: everything other than Him is a created being like me, not fit for lordship, so I would not become a servant of one of His servants.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, I will not rely upon anyone but Him, nor turn in repentance to anyone but Him, because He is the Lord of all things, its Sovereign, and to Him belong creation and command. In this verse there is the command to sincere worship and reliance (tawakkul). Just as the verse before it included sincere worship of Him without partner, this meaning is often paired with the other. Like His saying, Exalted is He, guiding His servants to say: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5], and His saying: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud: 123], and His saying: ﴿Say: "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him and upon Him we have relied"﴾ [al-Mulk: 29], and His saying: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity but Him, so take Him as a trustee (wakil)﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 9], and similar verses.

﴿And every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾

Ibn Kathir said: It is a report about what occurs on the Day of Resurrection, from God's recompense, His judgment and His justice: that souls are only repaid for their deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. And that no one's sin is carried by another. This is part of His justice, Exalted is He.

Abu al-Su'ud said: They used to say to the Muslims: "Follow our way, and let us bear your sins." This may mean: "let what you have done of sins be written against us, not against you," or it may mean: "let us bear on the Day of Resurrection what has been written against you of sins." So this is a rebuttal of it according to the first meaning: no offense of any soul is committed except against itself. It is impossible that its origin lies with one person and its burden falls upon another, so that what you mentioned could come about. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾, is a rebuttal of it according to the second meaning: on that Day no burdened soul will bear the load of another soul, so that your statement could be valid.

Note:

Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: This verse is a foundation for the principle that no one is held accountable for the act of another. Aisha used it to refute the one who said that the dead is punished for the weeping of the living over him. Al-Bukhari transmitted it. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from her that she was asked about the child of fornication, and she said: "He bears nothing of the sin of his parents," and she recited this verse.

Al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: The saying of Him, Exalted is He, ﴿and every soul earns only against itself﴾ is cited as proof that the disposal of Zayd over Amr is not binding except where evidence establishes it. Ibn al-Faras said: Those who denied that the prayer of the follower is linked to the prayer of the imam cited it as evidence.

Some of the Zaydis said: The saying of Him, Exalted is He, ﴿and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾ refers to the matter of the Hereafter. Thus the view that the children of polytheists are punished for the disbelief of their fathers is refuted, and it follows that the dead is not punished for the weeping of his family over him, since he has no cause for it. As for the matter of this world, this has been specified by the hadith of the 'aqilah (kin-group liability), and likewise the taking captive of the children of unbelievers and the like. End of quotation.

﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾, that is, your return after death on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ﴾, the truth being distinguished from falsehood. This verse is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "You will not be asked about what we committed of crime, nor will we be asked about what you do."﴾ [Saba: 25] ﴿Say: "Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us with truth, and He is the Judge, the All-Knowing."﴾ [Saba: 26]

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 6, verse 165:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[165] ﴿And it is He who has made you successors (khala'if) upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, that He may test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth﴾: khala'if is the plural of khalifah. That is, some of you succeed others in it, so that you populate it generation after generation, to dispose of it in various ways. ﴿And raised some of you above others in degrees﴾: that is, He differentiated among you in provision, character, beauty and ugliness, appearance, forms and colours, and He has wisdom in that. Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees that some of them may take others in service﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32], and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿See how We have preferred some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference﴾ [al-Isra': 21]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that He may test you in what He has given you﴾: that is, that He may try you concerning that with which He has favoured you, that is, He may put you to the test, so that He may examine the rich in his wealth and ask him about his gratitude, and the poor in his poverty and ask him about his patience. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, this world is sweet and green. Indeed, Allah appoints you as successors in it, and He will see how you act. So beware of the world and beware of women, for the first trial of the Children of Israel was with women." Ibn Kathir conveyed this.

Then, exalted is He, warned against His disobedience and encouraged obedience to Him by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment﴾: that is, for whoever disobeys Him and opposes His messengers. ﴿And indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: that is, for whoever allies himself with Him and follows His messengers.

Subtleties (lata'if):

The first: al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil": He cited His saying, ﴿made you successors of the earth﴾, by those who permitted it to be said of the Imam: "Khalifat Allah" (the successor of Allah). End of quote.

That is, based on one aspect of the verse, namely that the meaning is: He made you successors of Allah on the earth, disposing of it. The exegetes mentioned this. I had earlier preferred other than this aspect, because it is more precise and clearer, and Allah knows best.

The second: al-Qadi said: He described the punishment and did not attribute it to Himself, and He described His essence with forgiveness and joined to it the description of mercy, and He used the intensive pattern and the emphatic lam, as an indication that He, glorified and exalted is He, is Forgiving in His essence, and punishes only incidentally, abundant in mercy and exceeding in it, few in punishment and lenient in it. End of quote.

The third: Ibn Kathir said: The Exalted Truth frequently pairs these two attributes in the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6], and His saying: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful. And that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [al-Hijr: 49-50], along with other verses containing encouragement and warning.

Sometimes He calls His servants to Himself through desire, by describing Paradise and encouraging what is with Him; and sometimes He calls them through fear, by mentioning the Fire, its shackles and punishment, and the Resurrection and its terrors; and sometimes through both, so that each takes effect according to its suitability. May Allah make us among those who obey Him in what He commands and abandon what He forbids and warns against. Indeed, He is near and responsive.

With the praise of Allah, exalted is He, the discussion of "Mahasin al-Ta'wil" on Surat al-An'am has been completed. That was in the forenoon of Wednesday, 28 Rabi' al-Awwal, at the upper right window of the Sudda, in the Jami' al-Sananiyya, in the year 1321. A period of a month and a half had intervened, during which I stopped writing anything of this surah, from the end of the discussion of His saying, ﴿Those who associated will say﴾ [al-An'am: 148] onward, due to the intervening of my journey to Bayt al-Maqdis on 28 Muharram of the said year. After returning to my homeland on 8 Rabi' al-Awwal, I began from His saying, ﴿Say: Bring your witnesses﴾ [al-An'am: 150] onward, on 20 Rabi' al-Awwal, and the surah was completed on the date mentioned above. Praise be to Allah who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. By the pen of its compiler, Jamal al-Din al-Qasimi.
